review_units.title: fix(cron): re-arm daily/once schedules stranded by a crash mid-execution
review_units.head: 0cbc6d78a6db2935e51ca55c23f34d2f0a44d190

codex_findings.title: Consume interrupted occurrences after re-arming
codex_findings.detail: After an interrupted `once` or `daily` occurrence is re-armed and its retry completes, the old interrupted ledger row remains while the successful retry writes the same `due_at` back to `last_run`. On every subsequent Gateway start, this unrestricted scan finds the stale row and resets `last_run` again, causing a `once` action to execute after every restart and a daily action to duplicate if restarted before the next occurrence. Mark the interruption as reconciled or exclude occurrences that have a later terminal retry before resetting the schedule.

codex_findings.title: Avoid blindly retrying outcome-ambiguous actions
codex_findings.detail: If the Gateway dies after an action performs its external side effect but before `finish_run()` persists completion, the ledger is indistinguishable from a crash before dispatch and is marked `interrupted`. Resetting `last_run` automatically invokes that occurrence again, so non-idempotent scheduled actions such as `brief.deliver` can send duplicate notifications or repeat other external mutations. Only re-arm runs known not to have dispatched, or require result reconciliation or an idempotency key before retrying an outcome-ambiguous execution.

codex_findings.title: Refuse to re-arm an edited schedule
codex_findings.detail: When a schedule is edited after its occurrence is claimed but before the Gateway crashes, the interrupted run describes the old action and timing while the current `cron_schedules` row may describe a different job. This update checks only the shared ID, current type, and old cursor, so an interrupted `once` action A can cause newly configured action B to become due and execute after restart even though B was never the interrupted occurrence. Compare the current definition with the claimed execution intent, or otherwise preserve occurrence identity, before resetting it.

codex_findings.title: Stop startup when missed-occurrence reconciliation fails
codex_findings.detail: When the new reconciliation query or update raises, this handler logs the exception but still starts `_runner`; any previously claimed `once` schedule therefore remains permanently non-due until another restart happens to reconcile it successfully. Treat this like the preceding run-evidence reconciliation failure by returning or propagating the error rather than silently continuing without the promised recovery.

review_units.title: reconcile: preserve and integrate surviving Kitty work
review_units.head: d7e5a11ea8a09df417610ca103c520d23857f212

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed timeline timestamps
codex_findings.detail: If any required persisted timestamp is malformed or has an unsupported type, `_to_ts` silently converts it to Unix epoch zero. The activity remains present but is misordered at the end of the timeline, hiding storage corruption and making chronology inaccurate; raise with the source value/context instead of inventing a valid timestamp.

codex_findings.title: Timestamp grant revocations when they occur
codex_findings.detail: When an older grant is revoked, this entry reports `status="revoked"` but retains the grant's original creation timestamp, so a revocation performed today is sorted into the past and may disappear from a bounded timeline entirely. Use `revoked_at` for revoked entries so the projection reflects when the displayed activity actually occurred.

codex_findings.title: Filter failures before applying source limits
codex_findings.detail: For `filter="failures"`, each source is first truncated to `limit` entries and only then filtered. If, for example, 50 successful automation runs follow an older failed run, `/activity/timeline?filter=failures&limit=50` returns no automation failures even though one exists. Query or over-fetch failure rows before imposing the requested result limit.

codex_findings.title: Carry the source negative prompt into iteration batches
codex_findings.detail: For any succeeded source job with a `negative_prompt`, retry and duplicate omit it from the queued request. Stored plans do not contain this field, and `studio_generate` reads `req.negative_prompt` even when dispatching a stored plan, so the child renders with `None` instead of the source exclusions and is not an identical retry/duplicate. Include `ctx.negative_prompt` rather than silently replacing it with the request-model default.

codex_findings.title: Lock iteration to the source execution route
codex_findings.detail: The queued retry/duplicate request contains the stored plan and character fields but no source provider or model lock. If the plan's preferred recipe has become unavailable—or its recipe metadata changed—`studio_generate` falls through `auto_route` to another available recipe, while this module estimated and advertised the source provider. An iteration can therefore run on a different provider/model with different cost and policy behavior; fail when the original route cannot be reproduced instead of silently falling back.

codex_findings.title: Apply modifications before queuing the render
codex_findings.detail: When a user submits any `/modify` change, `after_ctx` is passed to `_enqueue_plan_batch`, but the batch still carries the original `plan_id`; `studio_generate` explicitly ignores request prompt/character/recipe fields whenever a plan is present, while seed, dimensions, steps, guidance, sampler, scheduler, and model are not accepted at all. The endpoint therefore reports the requested diff and may incur generation cost while rendering the approved plan unchanged; reject modifications until the dispatch path supports them, or persist and execute a genuinely modified plan.

codex_findings.title: Resolve artifacts before offering Use in chat
codex_findings.detail: This new action only appends the artifact's metadata ID to the composer. `streamChat` still sends ordinary text-only message bodies, and the gateway records `attachment_ids` in chat lifecycle evidence without loading the artifact or constructing image/text content for the model, so the model cannot actually use the selected artifact and the nonstandard top-level field may instead be rejected upstream. Resolve artifact content into the completion request, or expose the action as unavailable.

codex_findings.title: Fetch each project's actual stored next step
codex_findings.detail: This replaces the exact per-project `/projects/{id}/next` queries with the Home-oriented `/projects/next-steps` projection. That backend filters out archived projects and, when life projects exist, intentionally includes at most one Kitty self-development project, so valid stored steps for other rows are displayed as “no next step generated yet.” Use the per-project endpoint here, or add a batch endpoint that returns every requested project ID rather than the curated Home feed.

codex_findings.title: Attach lineage before registering the canonical artifact
codex_findings.detail: Every runner registers the canonical artifact before `studio_generate` returns, so this post-generation `set_parent` updates only the image-job row. For a text-to-image retry, the canonical artifact permanently records no iteration parent; for an image edit, it records the original edit anchor while the job row is overwritten to point at the retry source. Library and job provenance therefore disagree, so lineage must be supplied before artifact registration or the artifact metadata must be updated atomically.

codex_findings.title: Redact sensitive snapshots from undo history
codex_findings.detail: When `forget_memory_with_undo` handles a memory with `sensitivity="sensitive"`, it records the complete pre-forget snapshot, including its text, and this endpoint returns that snapshot unchanged. A caller with the memory ID can therefore retrieve the forgotten sensitive text even though `undo()` explicitly refuses to resurface it; redact sensitive `before`/`after` payloads from history or refuse history access for those entries.

codex_findings.title: Reject unknown entity types in undo history
codex_findings.detail: When a caller misspells `entity_type`, `list_history` skips the `ENTITY_TYPES` validation used by `record` and returns an empty 200 response, making an invalid request indistinguishable from an entity with no history. Validate the type before querying so unavailable evidence is not silently hidden.

codex_findings.title: Clear optional character fields when restoring null snapshots
codex_findings.detail: If a character originally has no description, preferred recipe, or tags and an update supplies those fields, the snapshot contains `None`; `_restore` passes that value to `update_character`, where `None` means “leave unchanged.” The undo call reports success while the newly added values remain, so restoration needs an explicit clear sentinel or direct support for setting nullable fields back to null.

codex_findings.title: Append a restoration event when undo succeeds
codex_findings.detail: After any successful undo, the restored mutation is not appended to the journal; only the original entry's `undone` flag is updated. Consequently history cannot represent or timestamp the documented `A → B → A` chronology, and the supposedly append-only audit trail is mutated in place without recording the restoration. Record the restored state as a new journal event while marking the source undo as consumed.

codex_findings.title: Route live mutations through the journal wrappers
codex_findings.detail: The live mutation endpoints never call these wrappers: the memory delete/correct routes still call `explicit_memory` directly, the loop toggle route calls `cron.toggle`, and both anchor routes call `image_sessions` directly. Consequently ordinary user mutations create no `undo_journal` row, so `/undo/history` stays empty and users never receive a journal ID that `/undo/{journal_id}` can restore; integrate journaling at those owning mutation seams.

review_units.title: fix(chat): expose only curated live models
review_units.head: 038ffe2d2a42bd28b26d156c38a3c1ced249309a

codex_findings.title: Include the runtime manifest in the gateway retry
codex_findings.detail: When `/runtime/manifest` alone fails or times out, this gate disables chat even if `/api/models` and `/models/picker` succeeded. The recovery control rendered by `StatusBar` calls `retryGatewayBootstrap`, but that callback invalidates `['models']`, `['brief']`, and several dashboard keys while omitting the `['runtime-manifest', projectId]` key used by `useGatewayRuntimeManifest`; clicking retry therefore leaves the failing prerequisite untouched and the composer blocked until the 15-second periodic refetch. Invalidate `['runtime-manifest']` as part of this recovery action.

codex_findings.title: Report an empty runtime intersection as unavailable
codex_findings.detail: When the independently fetched `/api/models` and `/runtime/manifest` snapshots have no IDs in common—for example, while LiteLLM routes are being reconfigured—`availableModels` becomes empty and `modelUnavailable` disables every send path, but `modelGateway.live` remains true. This prop therefore stays false, leaving the user with a disabled composer and no status or retry control until a periodic refetch happens; pass the full `modelUnavailable` condition into `StatusBar` (once loading is complete) so this fail-closed state is visible and recoverable.

codex_findings.title: Keep the hermetic chat gateway compatible with fail-closed sending
codex_findings.detail: When `npm run test:smoke:hermetic` runs, `playwright.hermetic.config.ts` starts `tests/support/hermetic_gateway.py`, which mounts the chat/completions routers but does not expose `/models/picker` or `/runtime/manifest`. Those requests therefore fail, `modelUnavailable` remains true, and this newly disabled composer prevents `chat-real-gateway.spec.ts` from sending the turn it is meant to verify. Mount deterministic picker/runtime routes in that hermetic gateway—or provide equivalent local route stubs—before making model availability a prerequisite for the test’s primary action.

codex_findings.title: Preserve chat through a configured direct provider
codex_findings.detail: When LiteLLM discovery is unavailable but the user has selected a configured direct provider, `/api/models` returns 502 and the runtime manifest reports its LiteLLM model fact as unknown, making `modelUnavailable` true and disabling every send here. The completion path nevertheless supports this degraded mode: `selected_provider_name()` and `call_selected_provider()` dispatch directly to the selected OpenAI, AgentRouter, or other provider without LiteLLM, while `compose_manifest()` catches the failed LiteLLM probe. Determine sendability from the selected provider path as well, rather than blocking a supported recovery route solely because the LiteLLM catalogue cannot be read.

codex_findings.title: Preserve picker failure details in the recovery message
codex_findings.detail: When `/models/picker` returns a status such as 503 or an invalid payload, `fetchGatewayModels()` includes that concrete cause in `modelError`, but this branch replaces it with a hard-coded category message, so the recovery UI still hides the status or validation failure needed to diagnose the outage. Fresh evidence at the exact head is that `modelStatusMessage()` now receives the detailed error but discards everything after `Model details unavailable`; preserve the returned detail in the displayed message.

codex_findings.title: Show blocked model state without waiting for rerenders
codex_findings.detail: When `/runtime/manifest` fails or reports unavailable after `/api/models` succeeds, `modelUnavailable` disables the composer but `modelGateway.error` remains null, so this render-count threshold hides the status and retry control until two unrelated rerenders happen; a stable production render can remain blocked with no explanation indefinitely. Derive confirmation from query failures or elapsed/retry state rather than the number of times React happens to render the component.

codex_findings.title: Bound the curated-picker request with a timeout
codex_findings.detail: When `/api/models` completes but `/models/picker` leaves its connection open, this new awaited fetch has neither a timeout nor an abort signal, so `fetchGatewayModels()` never settles and the React Query model state remains pending instead of falling back or refreshing. The preceding model probe is deliberately bounded to eight seconds; route this request through an equivalent timeout so a stalled picker fails visibly rather than blocking model availability indefinitely.

codex_findings.title: Report picker failures instead of claiming live metadata
codex_findings.detail: When `/api/models` succeeds but `/models/picker` returns an error or invalid payload, this catch silently substitutes `MODELS` and the following return still sets `fromLiveGateway: true` and `error: null`. `KittyContext` derives its model gateway health directly from those fields, so the UI reports healthy curated availability while hiding the picker failure and potentially omitting configured routes absent from the static fallback; preserve the safe fallback if desired, but propagate the failure state and cause.

codex_findings.title: Surface picker failures separately from gateway outages
codex_findings.detail: When `/api/models` and the runtime manifest remain healthy but `/models/picker` errors or times out, this result is reduced by `page.tsx` to `gatewayOffline`, and `StatusBar` displays only “gateway offline”; the detailed model error returned here is never shown. This misidentifies a picker-only failure and hides what failed from the user, so pass the model-availability error through and present a picker-specific recovery state. Exact-head product acceptance is `BLOCKED: reviewer infrastructure`: SHA `6f3721048502ce9742ef982cf270fef87c48676c` built and the 22 focused tests passed, but no executable Playwright or system browser was installed, so the required desktop/mobile running-product interactions and screenshots could not be performed.

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed picker presets before enabling them
codex_findings.detail: When `/models/picker` returns schema version 1 with a `presets` array containing malformed or unexpected entries, `fetchModelPicker` accepts it because it validates only the array itself, and this line trusts each entry’s `configured`, `route`, and label fields. If `/api/models` contains the same provider/internal alias—as LiteLLM discovery commonly does—a malformed preset naming that alias survives the intersection, marks availability live, appears in the human-facing picker, and can be dispatched. Validate every preset and its curated role/route contract before returning `fromLiveGateway: true`; otherwise treat the entire picker response as unavailable.

codex_findings.title: Honor the environment-level AgentRouter disable flag
codex_findings.detail: When `KITTY_DISABLE_AGENTROUTER=1` and AgentRouter is the saved active provider with a configured key, `/api/providers` still reports it as `configured: true` and `disabled: false`, so this predicate marks model availability live and enables the composer. The completion path explicitly rejects the same state in `selected_provider_name()` as “disabled by environment,” meaning every enabled send is guaranteed to fail even though the UI claims a live route; include that disable signal in provider availability before declaring the direct route ready.

codex_findings.title: Fail closed for a disabled selected provider
codex_findings.detail: When AgentRouter is the saved active provider, `KITTY_DISABLE_AGENTROUTER=1`, and the LiteLLM model endpoints are healthy, `isDirectProviderReady()` correctly returns false but this function simply falls through to the curated/runtime intersection and returns `live: true`. The composer is therefore enabled even though `selected_provider_name()` rejects every send before LiteLLM dispatch; fresh evidence at the exact head is that `/api/providers` now exposes the disable flag, but the availability policy uses that result only as a positive fallback and never as a veto for an explicitly selected provider that is not ready.

codex_findings.title: Disable sending when the curated intersection is empty
codex_findings.detail: When the runtime list and curated gateway list have no route in common—for example, LiteLLM currently exposes only internal aliases—this filter produces an empty `availableModels` array while `modelGateway.live` can remain true. The reconciliation effect explicitly retains the stale `activeModel` when the array is empty, and `InputBar` is disabled only while streaming, so the user can send a turn using an alias that the live availability data just rejected even though the picker says “no live models available”; treat an empty intersection as unavailable and prevent dispatch until a live route exists.

codex_findings.title: Clear stale one-shot overrides when the shortlist changes
codex_findings.detail: Unlike the already-fixed empty-intersection path, a recovery to a non-empty but changed curated shortlist re-enables the composer without reconciling `overrideModel`. For example, select `kitty-code` as the next-message override, let picker availability degrade, then restore it with only `kitty-small`: `availableModels` excludes `kitty-code`, but the override chip persists and `handleSend` passes that stale model directly to `runStream`. Reconcile or clear the override whenever it is absent from the new live shortlist so recovery cannot dispatch a route the picker has withdrawn.

codex_findings.title: Stub the runtime manifest in the standalone smoke test
codex_findings.detail: When `npm run test:smoke` runs `chat.spec.ts`, `playwright.config.ts` starts only Next and the shared fixture stubs only `/proxy/health`; this setup stubs `/api/models` and `/models/picker` but not `/runtime/manifest`. The new page gate requires `runtimeQuery.isSuccess`, so `modelUnavailable` remains true, the `InputBar` textarea is disabled, and the test's `input.fill('hello')` fails instead of verifying accessibility. Add a healthy runtime-manifest stub containing the available model to this standalone setup.

codex_findings.title: Isolate dotenv reads in AgentRouter tests
codex_findings.detail: When tests run in a configured checkout whose repository `.env` contains either AgentRouter key, this new direct `dotenv_values()` read bypasses the existing `load_dotenv` stubs: `test_resolve_agentrouter_key_missing_returns_empty` then returns the real key instead of `""`, and the keyless-provider fixtures can treat AgentRouter as configured. This makes the suite depend on the developer's secrets and can exercise a provider path those tests intend to exclude; update the affected tests/fixtures to stub `dotenv_values` (or inject the dotenv source) as well.

codex_findings.title: Preserve live AgentRouter key rotation
codex_findings.detail: When the AgentRouter token originates in the repository `.env` and is rotated while the gateway remains running, `_call_provider()` first calls `load_dotenv()`, which caches the original token in `os.environ`; this loop then returns that cached value before consulting `dotenv_values()`. Unlike the previous `load_dotenv(override=True)` behavior, subsequent calls keep using the revoked token until restart despite `_call_provider()` promising dotenv changes take effect live, so resolve ambient process credentials without allowing a value previously loaded from dotenv to mask the current AgentRouter token.

codex_findings.title: Stop reusing keys removed from dotenv
codex_findings.detail: When an AgentRouter key was previously copied into `os.environ` by `load_dotenv()` and is then removed or blanked in `.env` while Gateway remains running, `dotenv_values()` finds no current key and this fallback silently returns the stale, potentially revoked credential. Fresh evidence at the exact head is that replacement rotation is covered, but deletion/revocation still leaves `/api/providers` reporting AgentRouter configured and dispatches the old token until restart; distinguish dotenv-cached values from independently supplied process credentials instead of falling back to the cached value.

codex_findings.title: Isolate dotenv in the authentication-state test
codex_findings.detail: When a developer's repository `.env` contains either AgentRouter key, the dotenv-first resolver returns that real value rather than `runtime-agentrouter-key`, so this assertion fails and the test reads a personal credential. Fresh evidence at the exact head is that `dotenv_values` is now stubbed in the earlier resolver tests and provider fixtures, but this newly added authentication-state test still stubs only `load_dotenv`; stub the direct dotenv read here as well.

review_units.title: fix: finish remaining trust and runtime loops
review_units.head: 4ed7b5df744587a318cac583efa3637ae472264f

codex_findings.title: Raise the trivial cap above the required runtime context
codex_findings.detail: For trivial-tier turns, the 3,000-byte cap is smaller than the required runtime block itself: the current local `compact_runtime_context()` serializes to about 4,698 bytes before adding the bundle, tool guard, or user message. Because `_fit_final_model_messages()` refuses to clip runtime truth, an ordinary short request such as `hi` returns 413; the existing chat-completions tests reproduce this across normal streaming and non-streaming paths. Reserve enough space for the actual required blocks or derive the tier cap from their measured size.

codex_findings.title: Apply the cap after adding runtime system blocks
codex_findings.detail: In the main `/chat/completions` flow, `gateway/routes/completions.py` appends `compact_runtime_context(runtime_manifest)` and, normally, `_NO_TOOL_EXECUTOR_SYSTEM` after `assemble_context()` returns. When the fitted blocks consume this advertised cap, those unbudgeted system blocks immediately push the actual model-visible system prompt beyond it, so the change does not prevent the provider overflow it is intended to bound; reserve space for these blocks or enforce the cap on the final system prompt.

codex_findings.title: Enforce token caps with token-aware accounting
codex_findings.detail: Multiplying the advertised token limit by a fixed four characters does not bound tokens for CJK text, emoji, minified data, or other content that tokenizes near one character per token. For example, a standard-tier bundle can pass the 32,000-character check while consuming roughly 32,000 tokens rather than the claimed 8,000, so sufficiently non-English user context, objectives, memories, or enrichments can still overflow the provider context window; use tokenizer-aware accounting or a genuinely conservative bound.

codex_findings.title: Reconcile memory evidence after context clipping
codex_findings.detail: When the memory block exceeds its allocation, `_fit_context_blocks()` truncates the text placed in `system`, but `injected_memory_items` still contains every item selected before that second budget pass. The completion route then exposes those full records in the memory trailer and durable lifecycle ledger as the exact evidence used by the model, even when later records—or most of a record—never reached the prompt; filter or truncate the evidence against the final rendered system content.

codex_findings.title: Surface context clipping through the production warning path
codex_findings.detail: Whenever `_fit_context_blocks()` clips a block, the warning is placed only in the new `context_budget` field while `ContextBundle.warnings` remains unchanged; the production completion route neither reads nor logs `context_budget`, so prompt instructions can be truncated with no observable warning despite the claimed clipping receipt. Add these warnings to the established warning/logging path or explicitly propagate the receipt from production callers.

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed snooze instants instead of suppressing them
codex_findings.detail: When `/insight-loop/insight/{item_id}/respond` receives a nonempty but malformed `snooze_until` such as `not-a-date`, the route persists it without validation and this helper converts the parse failure into `False`. Every later due sweep then silently leaves the insight snoozed forever, with no warning or recovery path; validate the instant before persisting it or surface corrupt stored values as errors.

codex_findings.title: Parse snooze instants before comparing them
codex_findings.detail: For valid ISO datetimes with a non-UTC offset, lexical ordering does not represent chronological ordering: a snooze until `2026-01-02T08:00:00-08:00` is 16:00 UTC, but at 12:00 UTC this comparison sees `08` before `12` and returns the insight four hours early. The new `mark_returned()` guard uses the same string comparison, so parse and normalize both values to aware datetimes before deciding that a snooze elapsed.

codex_findings.title: Propagate tail-read failures before deduping
codex_findings.detail: When an existing push log cannot be opened or read, this converts the `OSError` into an empty history, so `_already_sent()` treats unavailable evidence as proof that no matching notification was sent and may deliver a duplicate. The same helper also makes prefetch history failures indistinguishable from an empty history; preserve the missing-file case, but propagate or explicitly surface actual read failures.

codex_findings.title: Reject corrupt UTF-8 in audit tails
codex_findings.detail: If a push or prefetch history file contains an invalid UTF-8 byte from corruption or a torn external write, `errors="replace"` silently substitutes U+FFFD instead of surfacing the damaged evidence. A JSON line containing that byte can still parse successfully and be trusted with altered fields—for example, a changed dedupe key can permit a duplicate push—whereas the previous strict text decoding raised; decode strictly or explicitly reject and report corrupt lines.

codex_findings.title: Generate collision-proof IDs before preserving old chunks
codex_findings.detail: When a source is force-refreshed within the same second as its previous ingestion, the timestamp-based IDs at line 156 equal `existing_ids`; with the pinned ChromaDB 1.5.8, `Collection.add()` leaves records with duplicate IDs unchanged rather than replacing them, after which this new delete removes those old records. The function then reports a successful replacement even though every colliding chunk has disappeared, so generate unique replacement IDs before adding and deleting the snapshot.

codex_findings.title: Keep cron evidence attached to threaded life actions
codex_findings.detail: If `cron.stop()` cancels the runner while either wrapper is awaiting `asyncio.to_thread()`, cancellation ends the coroutine but does not stop the worker thread. The reflection/provider work can therefore finish and send its push after `automation_actions.run_action()` has lost control, leaving the durable run in `running` state to be reconciled as interrupted on restart; retrying that apparently interrupted run can duplicate the external notification. Track and await the worker through shutdown or otherwise prevent cancellation from separating the side effect from its run evidence.

codex_findings.title: Propagate push-log rotation failures
codex_findings.detail: When rotation fails because a retained file cannot be unlinked or renamed, this catches the `OSError` and lets `_log_attempt()` continue as though bounded audit maintenance succeeded. If the active file remains appendable, it can then grow without the advertised bound while callers still receive successful notification results; surface the rotation failure to the caller rather than swallowing it.

codex_findings.title: Preserve tool-continuation messages after the last user
codex_findings.detail: For an Open WebUI tool continuation shaped as `user → assistant(tool_calls) → tool(result)`, the last user is selected as `current_user`, but the history slice ends before it, so both messages after that user are omitted from the upstream payload. The model receives the original question again without its tool call or result and can repeat the call indefinitely; retain and budget the post-user continuation as an atomic tool exchange.

codex_findings.title: Keep historical tool exchanges atomic while trimming
codex_findings.detail: When an older assistant `tool_calls` message exceeds the remaining budget but its following tool-result message is small, this per-message reverse scan retains the tool result and drops the assistant call that introduced its `tool_call_id`. The resulting upstream transcript is invalid for OpenAI-compatible providers and can turn an otherwise valid long tool conversation into a 400 response; group each assistant call with its tool responses and keep or drop the exchange together.

codex_findings.title: Preserve unavailable runtime facts in the prompt projection
codex_findings.detail: When a connection or approval probe reports `unknown`, `unavailable`, or `degraded`, this projection now ends after `inference` and silently omits `connections`, `tools`, and `approvals`, so chat turns cannot distinguish missing capability evidence from a healthy runtime. This also contradicts the compact-projection contract in `docs/CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.md:1143-1149`; retain at least each section's compact state and reason rather than hiding it.

codex_findings.title: Reject symlinks in every destination ancestor
codex_findings.detail: If `.next` itself is a symlink to an external build tree, none of the listed destination paths is itself a symlink, so these checks pass and the later `rm -rf` commands delete `.next/static` or `public` in that external tree. This can arise from a stale linked build directory even without a symlink at one of the four checked leaves; validate the canonical destination remains below the real UI directory or reject `.next` and every ancestor before deletion.

review_units.title: fix(chat): reconcile interrupted turns on restart
review_units.head: 999372b39c698c5ad61ea23520894f3567813711

codex_findings.title: Materialize recovery shells before terminalizing their turns
codex_findings.detail: If the process exits or any `chats_store` operation raises after `reconcile_interrupted_turns()` commits but before the shell-upsert loop completes, the next startup cannot repair the ledger-only chat: `list_running_conversations()` now returns nothing because its turn is already terminal, while `/chats` still has no shell to expose. The fresh evidence at the current head is the split, non-atomic ordering here combined with the running-only selector, which makes a transient failure in this startup pass permanently recreate the earlier reload-discovery problem.

codex_findings.title: Persist the ledger's actual model in recovered shells
codex_findings.detail: For a ledger-only first turn sent through any non-default model, startup writes `kitty-default` into the compatibility chat even though the lifecycle attempt records the actual requested model. That fabricated value is returned by `/chats` and consumed directly by `chronicle_service.model_usage()`, permanently misattributing the recovered session in usage analysis unless a later client save happens to replace it; project the recorded model or represent it as unavailable instead of inventing one.

codex_findings.title: Expose reconciled ledger-only chats to reload
codex_findings.detail: When the Gateway dies during the first turn of a newly created chat, no legacy chat row may exist: `handleSend()` starts the stream without persisting the chat, and `persistChat()` runs only after success or in the client-side error path, when the Gateway can still be unavailable (`gateway/kitty-chat/src/state/KittyContext.tsx:641-665`). This startup pass reconciles the normalized `chat_conversations` row, but reload discovery fetches `/proxy/chats`, which enumerates only `chats_store.list_chats()` and never ledger-only conversations (`gateway/routes/chats.py:47-50`). Consequently, the interrupted conversation and the new retryable record remain unreachable after reload; discovery or reconciliation needs to materialize these ledger-only chats.

codex_findings.title: Avoid promising retry on non-final interrupted turns
codex_findings.detail: When the same conversation has multiple in-flight turns, such as from two browser tabs, reconciliation inserts this “Tap retry” message for every orphan in turn order. The UI only supplies `onRetry` to the final assistant message in the conversation (`gateway/kitty-chat/src/components/KittyThread.tsx:115-118`), and its generic retry handler targets the latest user turn, so earlier interruption bubbles instruct the user to tap a control that does not exist. Either provide a per-turn retry path or use different recovery copy for interrupted turns that are not retryable.

codex_findings.title: Suppress the superseded interruption after retry
codex_findings.detail: When a user follows this new interruption bubble's retry action, the retry creates another lifecycle turn with the same `source_message_id`; however, `_recover_messages()` processes turns oldest-first and skips only the duplicate user row, while retaining assistant rows from both turns (`gateway/routes/chats.py:132-177`). After the retry succeeds and the page is reloaded, recovery therefore returns the interruption message immediately followed by the successful answer. Suppress assistant messages from superseded turns, or otherwise replace this placeholder when the turn is retried.

codex_findings.title: Compare retry eligibility against all later turns
codex_findings.detail: When two concurrent turns exist and the later turn finishes before the Gateway crashes while the earlier turn remains running, this query excludes the completed later turn, so the earlier orphan is treated as the latest sequence and receives “Tap retry.” After recovery, that bubble is not the final assistant message and therefore has no retry control (`gateway/kitty-chat/src/components/KittyThread.tsx:115-118`); the visible control instead retries the later user turn. Fresh evidence at the current head is that `latest_sequence` is computed only from `status = 'running'` rows rather than from every turn in the conversation.

codex_findings.title: Preserve attachments when replacing a retried turn
codex_findings.detail: When the interrupted user message had attachments, a successful UI retry creates the newer lifecycle row without them because `handleRetry` calls `runStream` without `attachmentIds` (`gateway/kitty-chat/src/state/KittyContext.tsx:697`). This `continue` then discards the entire original turn—including the user row that still contains the artifact IDs—in favor of the attachment-free retry row, so after reload the recovered user message no longer displays its original attachments.

review_units.title: fix(ui): one truthful status, in plain language
review_units.head: 4b8cb7e0ce8d60acd7cd6a0fa62ec0db63ea51fa

codex_findings.title: Replace the stale continuity checkpoint
codex_findings.detail: The committed handoff identifies `3e022bf` on `claude/kitty-power-run-l4dvwx` as the current head, but the reviewed artifact is `ae4e1d1`; its own invalidation condition is therefore already satisfied, while the file still reports the old PR and branch as current. Any session or tooling that consumes this checkpoint can inherit obsolete ownership and next-action state, so update it for the committed SHA or explicitly mark it superseded.

codex_findings.title: Expose Builder's data-quality detail
codex_findings.detail: For partial packet records or missing transition history, the supplied `detail` is discarded and replaced with “Open Builder for details,” even though this notice already renders inside the Builder surface and no detail is exposed there. Users therefore have neither the cause nor a valid route to it; retain a plain-language translation alongside the underlying count/cause or provide an actual details control.

codex_findings.title: Distinguish Builder activity from reply generation
codex_findings.detail: `useKittyState` also returns `working` whenever `builderActive` is true, so an active background Builder run with an idle chat makes this badge announce “Kitty is working on a reply.” That invents a chat operation that is not happening; either represent Builder activity with a distinct state or choose this reply-specific description from actual streaming state.

codex_findings.title: Give the labelled badge a nameable ARIA role
codex_findings.detail: A plain `span` maps to the generic ARIA role, for which accessible-name calculation is prohibited, so assistive technology may ignore `aria-label` even though Testing Library can locate the attribute. The new descriptive name therefore does not reliably reach screen-reader users; add an appropriate role such as `status` or provide visually hidden descriptive text instead.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the degraded domain's actual reason
codex_findings.detail: When a health domain is degraded and the user selects “explain,” this now discards `domain.reason` and shows only a generic restatement of its status. The backend supplies actionable distinctions such as a failed schedule lookup or an embedding runtime HTTP response, so the operator-facing health surface can no longer explain what actually failed despite being explicitly designed to do so; translate the reason if needed, but do not replace it with status-only copy.

codex_findings.title: Surface failure to persist the PWA dismissal
codex_findings.detail: When `localStorage.setItem` throws—for example because browser storage is blocked or unavailable—the handler silently dismisses the banner in memory anyway. The user is given no indication that the requested persistent dismissal failed, and the banner returns after reload; report the storage failure visibly or otherwise distinguish a session-only dismissal instead of silently claiming success.

codex_findings.title: Keep connection health separate from reply outcome
codex_findings.detail: While the runtime manifest is still loading, `page.tsx` supplies `unknown`, and degraded or stale connections also reach this branch; all of them are converted to `broke`, causing `StateBadge` to claim “reply failed” even when the last reply succeeded or no reply has occurred. Preserve `catState` here and let the adjacent runtime badge report connection health instead.

codex_findings.title: Point authentication failures to a real recovery path
codex_findings.detail: Any gateway 401 or 403 now instructs the user to check a gateway secret in Settings, but the inspected `SettingsPanel.tsx` has no gateway-secret control; proxy configuration reads the secret from environment/repository configuration instead. Thus an authentication failure presents a recovery action the user cannot perform, and a genuine authorization-denied 403 is also misdiagnosed as a secret problem.

codex_findings.title: Do not label application errors as connection failures
codex_findings.detail: The fallback covers non-network failures such as the invalid-payload errors thrown by `fetchTodos` and `fetchSessionContext`, yet it always says something went wrong “reaching Kitty.” In those cases Kitty answered and returned malformed data, so the shared translator now creates a false connectivity diagnosis across every newly routed surface; distinguish response/validation failures from actual transport failures.

codex_findings.title: Restrict setup-jargon filtering to technical projects
codex_findings.detail: The unqualified `tracker` pattern is applied to every project kind, so legitimate life-project content such as “set up a habit tracker” or “review sleep tracker results” is replaced with the false claim that no project details are connected; the same corruption affects generated next steps. Gate this setup filter by project kind or narrow it to actual internal tracker terminology.

review_units.title: Make Work actionable and Builder actually run
review_units.head: 9018d4696b1ec5b4af945437fe813ee445526c88

codex_findings.title: Keep pushes behind explicit authorization
codex_findings.detail: When an agent follows `CLAUDE.md` as its working authority, these lines instruct it to push a branch and open a PR before asking Jacob. Branch protection does not prevent either remote mutation, and the root contract explicitly prohibits pushing without authorization, so routine completed work could be published unexpectedly. Preserve local commits as the default and require explicit permission before any push.

codex_findings.title: Do not stamp dirty UI builds as clean HEAD
codex_findings.detail: When `make ui-build` runs with uncommitted changes under `gateway/kitty-chat`, Next compiles the working-tree contents, but this line records only the clean commit SHA. `kitty status` then presents that commit as the build source while the running artifact can contain arbitrary uncommitted code, hiding precisely the provenance evidence this change is intended to provide. Refuse dirty relevant inputs or include a dirty marker or tree digest in the stamp.

codex_findings.title: Honor the new CAD 2 total spend ceiling
codex_findings.detail: This commit records a hard ceiling of CAD 2 total in `config/PREFERENCES.md`, but the new Mission instead authorizes CAD 6 per week and the referenced `config/compute_governor.json` still enforces that larger weekly amount. Any explicitly paid Builder run can therefore remain governor-approved after crossing the newly recorded total authorization. Resolve the conflicting authority and lower the runtime governor before allowing paid execution.

codex_findings.title: Terminate the detached process group on claim timeout
codex_findings.detail: If a launch takes longer than ten seconds to claim, `terminate()` signals only the `kitty` Bash wrapper. That wrapper invokes the Python Builder CLI without `exec`, so its child can survive the shell's termination, retain the dispatch-lock descriptor, and later claim or run the task after the supervisor has reported failure. Signal the new session's process group and wait for termination before returning the error.

codex_findings.title: Move the launchctl probe off the FastAPI event loop
codex_findings.detail: The async `/builder/supervisor` route calls `control_plane_summary()` synchronously, and this newly added field runs `launchctl` with a timeout of up to two seconds. Because Work polls the endpoint every ten seconds, a slow or wedged `launchctl` can repeatedly block the Gateway event loop and stall unrelated chat and API requests; run this probe in a worker thread/asynchronously or cache it outside the request path.

codex_findings.title: Preserve unknown supervisor state when its query fails
codex_findings.detail: When `/builder/supervisor` is pending or returns an error while `/work` still succeeds, this defaults the unavailable state to `false`; eligible rows consequently say Builder is stopped and offer a start action, while the supervisor failure itself is never displayed. Treat the state as unknown and surface the query error instead of inventing a stopped state from missing evidence.

codex_findings.title: Do not requeue attempt-exhausted packets
codex_findings.detail: When `next_action === 'exhausted'`, this offers the same `requeue` command as ordinary recovery, but `operator_release_task` only changes the queue state while `_exhausted_packet_ids` continues deriving exhaustion from the durable failed attempts. The command can therefore report success and leave the task queued, yet `next_packet` will permanently exclude it, so “Try again” never causes another attempt. Either provide a canonical budget-reset/override operation or explain that no retry is currently available.

codex_findings.title: Scope the row-level start action to its row
codex_findings.detail: When three or more initiatives are ready, pressing “Start Builder” on a particular row invokes the global supervisor tick, which deterministically launches only the first two initiatives by ID. The clicked row may therefore remain untouched while unrelated work starts and the UI reports success. Use a packet- or initiative-scoped start operation here, or present this only as a clearly global action outside the row.

codex_findings.title: Hide cancellation when the task state rejects it
codex_findings.detail: When `current_packet.task_state` is `running` or `pr_opened`, this still returns true because the initiative is nonterminal and has a task ID, but `operator_cancel_task` explicitly refuses both states. Active and awaiting-checks rows therefore show a “Cancel task” control that is guaranteed to fail; gate this on the projected task state or route active work through the supported run-cancellation operation.

codex_findings.title: Render cancellation independently of the primary action
codex_findings.detail: For real nonterminal projections such as `next_action: 'queued'` or `'await_review'`, `rowAction` returns `kind: 'none'`, so this outer condition suppresses the entire action container—including the `canCancel(item)` button. The canonical queue state machine permits cancelling queued and awaiting-review tasks, but users cannot invoke that supported action from Work; render cancellation whenever `canCancel` is true even if no primary action exists.

codex_findings.title: Do not promise project cancellation for one task
codex_findings.detail: Each Work row represents an initiative, and the confirmation names the initiative title and promises that “It will stop and stay stopped,” but the command cancels only `current_packet.task_id`. In a multi-packet initiative with another independent eligible packet, the supervisor can continue running that other packet immediately after this succeeds. Either pause/cancel the initiative or label the control and confirmation as cancelling only the selected packet.

codex_findings.title: Keep manual dispatch available while another run is active
codex_findings.detail: When one run is active while `eligible_now > 0`, this branch hides the global tick control even though a tick supports up to two launches, and ready rows claim Builder will pick them up later. Each detached `run-packet` handles only its own packet, so with `scheduler_enabled === false` the remaining eligible work is not dispatched after capacity frees unless the user returns later; keep the global action available when eligible work remains or make the message reflect the unscheduled state.

codex_findings.title: Translate supervisor failures before displaying them
codex_findings.detail: When a tick fails because the launcher or worker adapter is missing, the route returns the exception text in `error`, and this line displays that value verbatim. The added API test demonstrates a normal payload such as `canonical worker adapter missing: scripts/worker.sh`, so the Work surface exposes internal component names and paths despite the Mission's explicit prohibition on raw server errors and internal service names. Show a bounded plain-language explanation and put the raw detail behind technical details.

codex_findings.title: Distinguish an idle scheduled supervisor from a stopped one
codex_findings.detail: In an installation where the documented launchd supervisor is loaded but currently between its 15-minute ticks, `active_runs` is empty, so the API sets `running` false and this banner claims “Builder is stopped” and “Nothing moves until you start it.” That inference is false: the next scheduled tick can move work without this button. The status needs a separate scheduler/service-enabled signal, or the UI must describe this state as idle rather than stopped.

codex_findings.title: Bound Builder action requests with a timeout
codex_findings.detail: If the Next proxy or Gateway accepts a connection but stops responding, this `fetch` has no abort timeout, so a retry, cancel, resume, or supervisor tick remains pending indefinitely and its button stays disabled as “Working…” or “Starting…”. The existing work snapshot request already uses `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`; apply the same bounded failure behavior to mutations so the operator receives an actionable error instead of a permanently hung control.

codex_findings.title: Allow supervisor ticks to finish before aborting
codex_findings.detail: Fresh evidence after the earlier timeout comment is that the new 8-second action timeout is shorter than the server's own operation contract: `_wait_for_durable_claim` allows 10 seconds per launch, and `tick` can perform two launches sequentially. If a child claims after eight seconds, the browser reports an abort even though Builder can subsequently launch the work successfully; use a tick-specific timeout exceeding the worst-case server duration or make the endpoint return before waiting.

codex_findings.title: Reserve packets before acknowledging a tick
codex_findings.detail: When two `/builder/supervisor/tick` requests arrive back-to-back, the first `bs.tick()` releases `SupervisorLock` immediately after `Popen`, before the detached child reaches `claim_and_start_attempt`; the second request can therefore select and spawn the same still-queued packet, and both HTTP calls report it as started. The children also preflight the same worktree before queue fencing rejects one, so reserve or claim the selected packet durably while the supervisor lock is held before returning success.

codex_findings.title: Check cleanliness before every automatic UI rebuild
codex_findings.detail: Fresh evidence after the earlier Makefile provenance issue is that the newly added guard is invoked only when `BUILD_ID` is absent. If an existing build has a newer dirty input, or lacks `KITTY_SOURCE_SHA`, the later branches run `npm run build` and `record_build_source` without this check, compiling uncommitted code and stamping it as clean `HEAD`; invoke the guard before every rebuild path.

review_units.title: builder: implement agent operability and durable execution primitives
review_units.head: 6f3fce26bfe49e3d440020f8746138cefb7c0f1a

codex_findings.title: Run validation commands from explicit workflow steps
codex_findings.detail: When a new multi-step contract places its checks in each step's `validation_commands`, `run_contract` compiles and returns those commands but continues executing only the legacy top-level list. A failing step command is therefore absent from `command_results` and cannot make `passed` false, allowing `builder contract validate` to accept a workflow without running its declared checks. Aggregate the reachable steps' validation commands or explicitly reject step-local commands until an executor handles them.

codex_findings.title: Make idempotent receipt creation atomic
codex_findings.detail: When multiple workers request the same `(operation, idempotency_key)` concurrently, each can observe no existing row and attempt this insert; the loser receives a raw `sqlite3.IntegrityError` instead of the winner's durable receipt. This makes the idempotent request seam fail during an ordinary Builder collision, so handle the unique conflict by reloading and validating the committed row, or use an atomic insert-or-load operation.

codex_findings.title: Prevent stale verification from overwriting terminal evidence
codex_findings.detail: When two callers reconcile the same `unknown` invocation concurrently, one can record `VERIFICATION_APPLIED` and transition the receipt to `succeeded`, after which the other caller's stale `VERIFICATION_UNKNOWN` result executes this unconditional update. The durable row then says `succeeded` while its verification evidence says `unknown`; make this update conditional on `status = 'unknown'` and treat a lost race by reloading the terminal receipt.

codex_findings.title: Persist an unknown outcome when result serialization fails
codex_findings.detail: When `execute()` completes its side effect but returns a non-JSON-serializable result, serialization occurs after the guarded execution block, so `_transition` raises and leaves the receipt permanently `running` with no error. Subsequent calls refuse replay as though a worker were still active even though this invocation already returned; serialize inside an outcome-handling path and durably transition to `unknown` so the verifier can reconcile the potentially committed effect.

codex_findings.title: Enforce the ceiling for fallback candidates
codex_findings.detail: When either fallback list contains an unpriced or more expensive model, this accepts the slug without running the cost estimator; `resolve_paid_route` later projects only the primary worker/reviewer pair and compares that amount with the per-attempt ceiling. The resulting routing plan can therefore authorize a fallback combination that cannot be priced or exceeds `max_projected_cost_cad`; price every candidate and enforce the ceiling against the most expensive permitted combination.

codex_findings.title: Reject an explicitly empty source tier
codex_findings.detail: When upstream supplies `source_tier=""`, this truthiness fallback silently replaces the invalid value with the target tier, producing a same-tier `continue` handoff instead of reporting malformed routing context. That can discard the required escalation/downshift context policy while the receipt falsely records a valid handoff; default only when the value is `None` and let `plan_handoff` reject empty strings.

codex_findings.title: Serialize the legacy policy-column migration
codex_findings.detail: When multiple Builder workers initialize the same legacy governor database concurrently, each can observe that `policy_json` is absent and then attempt this `ALTER TABLE`; after the first commits, another initializer fails with `sqlite3.OperationalError: duplicate column name: policy_json`. This can make workers fail during the first startup after upgrading an existing receipt store, so serialize the migration or recheck the schema after acquiring the write lock.

codex_findings.title: Validate improvement before persisting it
codex_findings.detail: When a caller supplies a deserialized or modified evaluation mapping, `improved=True` is trusted without checking that `absolute_lift == candidate_mean - baseline_mean`, that the lift is positive, or that it meets `minimum_lift`. Consequently, even a negative candidate result can be recorded as `capability_improvement` and promoted after repetition; recompute or reject inconsistent evaluation fields before writing durable learning evidence.

review_units.title: feat(runtime): harden Kitty reliability boundaries
review_units.head: 62f31a0f63859f0c52b856217b86b8711bd5e1df

codex_findings.title: Keep context health synchronized with later budget warnings
codex_findings.detail: The new `context_health` value is computed once from the assembler's current warnings, but the completions route subsequently appends `_fit_final_model_messages()` warnings to the same bundle. When that final pass clips the bundle system or drops history, `bundle.warnings` records the clipping while `context_health["budget_clipped"]` remains false, making the advertised receipt internally inconsistent; recompute the health receipt after warning mutation or provide a single method that updates both.

codex_findings.title: Surface MCP discovery failures instead of reporting healthy
codex_findings.detail: When the plugin registry fails or `.mcp.json` is malformed, `list_servers()` catches the exception and returns a partial or empty list; this new snapshot converts that into `configured_servers == 0` and `state == "available"`, so `_mcp_tools_source()` reports “no MCP servers configured” rather than a configuration failure. Propagate the discovery error or represent it as unavailable/degraded health so this path cannot silently turn broken configuration green.

codex_findings.title: Remove circuits for servers that are no longer configured
codex_findings.detail: When an open circuit's server is disabled or removed from configuration, this loop continues publishing the process-local circuit even though the server is absent from `configured`. Because `invoke()` returns `server_not_found` before touching breaker state, the stale entry can keep `/health/surface` degraded indefinitely until a process restart or manual reset; filter or clear circuits whose server is no longer configured.

codex_findings.title: Preserve timeout and cancellation when termination races with exit
codex_findings.detail: If the child exits after the `returncode` check but before `proc.terminate()`, asyncio can raise `ProcessLookupError` here. That cleanup exception then replaces the intended timeout result or the original `CancelledError`, so callers receive neither the real failure nor the promised cancellation propagation; tolerate the already-exited race and still await/reap the process.

codex_findings.title: Do not open the circuit for ordinary tool errors
codex_findings.detail: When a server returns a JSON-RPC error for caller-controlled input, such as invalid arguments or an application-level rejection, this records it as a dependency failure. Three such requests therefore open the circuit and block a subsequent valid invocation for the cooldown period even though the transport and server are healthy; only transient transport/server failures, or explicitly classified retryable tool errors, should contribute to the cutoff.

codex_findings.title: Reject responses that omit both result and error
codex_findings.detail: When a server returns a JSON object with neither `result` nor `error`—for example a truncated or unrelated JSON-RPC message—`response.get("result", {})` invents an empty successful result and clears the circuit. Treat the missing `result` member as an invalid response so malformed transport evidence cannot silently become success.

codex_findings.title: Capture and validate the tested SHA before repetitions
codex_findings.detail: Because pytest executes the live working tree but `_git_head()` is called only after every repetition, a dirty checkout or a commit/checkout occurring during the potentially long run produces a receipt that attributes results to a SHA whose contents were not necessarily tested. Capture the SHA before starting and reject dirty or changed state afterward, or run the scenarios from an immutable checkout of that SHA.

review_units.title: Kb mtg94d5b beb0
review_units.head: b19827d45660bb09006b3cb75735d750ffd553df

codex_findings.title: Add preflight to the command handler registry
codex_findings.detail: When a client posts `action="preflight"`, `dispatch_operator_command` checks `COMMAND_HANDLERS` before consulting this argument map, but that registry contains no `preflight` entry. Every request therefore returns `unknown action: preflight`, making the newly declared operation unreachable; register and implement its handler in the canonical command registry.

codex_findings.title: Make preserved final worktrees retryable after a grant
codex_findings.detail: When the last non-repairable attempt leaves a dirty worktree, this early exhaustion return preserves it but records no durable disposition that a later invocation can recover. After the operator grants another attempt and requeues the task, the new `run_packet` call has an empty `history`, passes `reuse_dirty_worktree=False`, and `run_worker` refuses the preserved tree as dirty, consuming the granted attempt as a crash; archive/reset it before the granted retry or durably rehydrate the prior disposition.

codex_findings.title: Clear locked worktree metadata when the path is absent
codex_findings.detail: When `git worktree add` times out after registering and locking its metadata but before the checkout path exists, this guard skips both `unlock` and `remove`. `git worktree prune` retains the locked entry, and the next add then fails with Git's `missing but locked worktree; use ... unlock and prune or remove` error, leaving the packet stuck until manual repair; clean the registered worktree even when its directory is absent and verify that cleanup succeeds.

codex_findings.title: Initialize a fresh governor ledger before preflight
codex_findings.detail: When `db_path` names a fresh database—as supported by the documented isolated-test-path argument, or on a first-run default—`reserve_from_ledger` immediately queries `work_receipts` without calling `init_db`. SQLite creates an empty file and then raises `OperationalError: no such table: work_receipts`, so preflight cannot return its estimate until some unrelated governor path initializes the schema.

codex_findings.title: Project routes using the governor's reserve floors
codex_findings.detail: When a risky or blocker packet is preflighted with the weekly reserve at or below `frontier_floor_ratio`, this branch always reports `frontier`; the actual `decide()` path downgrades to `cheap`, or defers at the hard floor. This can report `projected_route="frontier"` and `within_budget=true` even though execution will take a different action, so the projection should reuse the governor's reserve-floor decision logic.

review_units.title: docs(packets): the four-packet finish slate, re-verified at 295b92fc
review_units.head: f4c71ef89fb6d3a8e52892d7320cebb87c31798a

codex_findings.title: Export all records before replacing stores
codex_findings.detail: For an installation with more than 1,000 memories or journal entries, the mandated replace operation will turn a normal export/restore into data loss: `gateway/storage_sync.py:50` and `:54` cap both exported lists at 1,000, so replacing each store with that snapshot permanently deletes every omitted record. Extend this packet to make exports exhaustive (or explicitly fail when they cannot be) and add a greater-than-1,000-record round-trip criterion before enabling replacement semantics.

codex_findings.title: Name the preference store that must round-trip
codex_findings.detail: The packet is not self-contained enough to implement `the real preferences store`: this checkout has at least the standing user preferences in `config/PREFERENCES.md`, provider-routing preferences in `config/providers.json`, and scheduling/push preferences in `config/user_profile.json`, with different shapes and writers. A worker can legitimately choose only one, satisfy the vague non-empty-dict test, and continue silently omitting the preferences Jacob expected the backup to preserve. Name every authoritative preference source, its snapshot shape, and its import path in the objective and acceptance criteria.

codex_findings.title: Remove the shared test fence from independent packets
codex_findings.detail: `KT-RESTORE-01` has no dependency on either of the other packets but shares the broad `tests` fence with both, so independently dispatchable workers are authorized to modify the same paths. Both preflight and `kitty builder initiative validate` report these collisions, and `docs/packets/PACKET_STANDARD.md:141-143` requires packets that can run concurrently not to share a path. Narrow each packet to its named existing test files or add the required dependency edges before applying the initiative.

codex_findings.title: Require failed scheduled pushes to record a non-success status
codex_findings.detail: This criterion only proves that the scheduled action calls the push facade, not that its durable automation result reflects delivery. `deadline_watch.check_and_push()` catches push exceptions and returns a normal `{checked, pushed, skipped}` dict even when `pushed` is zero, while `automation_actions._normalize_result()` converts every non-`ActionResult` value to `completed`. With no configured channel or a transport failure, the newly wired deadline run will therefore claim completion despite delivering no warning. Require and test a `source_unavailable` or failed action result when no escalation was delivered.

codex_findings.title: Allow the required smoke specifications in the packet fence
codex_findings.detail: This Tier-2 requirement tells the Builder output to add a spec under `gateway/kitty-chat/tests/smoke/`, but `KT-AUTO-01` only permits the root `tests` directory and its four backend modules; `KT-DEADLINE-01` has the same mismatch for its required smoke spec. No existing smoke test covers either behavior, so a worker cannot produce the repository-required running-app proof without an irreparable scope violation. Include the smoke-test directory in each executable fence or assign that proof to a separate scoped packet.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the checkpoint-specific quiet-hours behavior
codex_findings.detail: The statement that existing quiet hours will prevent notification noise is not true for the function being scheduled: `deadline_watch.check_and_push()` sends every checkpoint as `kind="alert"`, while `push_to_jacob()` applies quiet hours only to `kind="info"`. The original deadline contract in `docs/packets/017-benefits-rails-urgent-sweep.md:91-96` calls for informational T-7/T-3 pushes and alert T-1/day-of pushes. Wiring the current function unchanged can therefore send early warnings during quiet hours; include restoring the checkpoint-specific kinds in this packet or stop claiming quiet-hours protection.

codex_findings.title: Fix the todo completion control before calling the panel complete
codex_findings.detail: `TodoPanel` passes its completion mutation through `WorkCard.onRetry`, and `WorkCard` consequently renders the only completion control with a rotate icon and the label `retry`. Mounting the panel as-is gives users no control identified as completing a pending todo, despite the packet claiming completion is already implemented and limiting the work to wiring. Include correcting this control and asserting its accessible label and mutation behavior in the packet.

codex_findings.title: Account for the monitor identifier mismatch before mounting
codex_findings.detail: Mounting `MonitorPanel` unchanged does not yield working removal: `/monitors` returns raw `web_monitor.list_watches()` rows whose identifier is `id`, while `MonitorPanel.tsx` keys rows and calls the delete mutation with `m.watch_id`. Existing monitors therefore render with undefined keys and removal requests target `/monitor/undefined`. Add the required frontend normalization or component correction to this packet instead of treating the panel as complete wiring-only work.

codex_findings.title: Stop negation matching from consuming later creation requests
codex_findings.detail: The arbitrary-word allowance after `without`, `rather than`, and similar prefixes can consume a later positive creation verb: for example, `Without delay implement a helper` is reduced to text with no creation verb, so `implies_new_file()` returns false. A file-only packet using that ordinary phrasing therefore passes with only a warning even though implementing the helper may require a new file and permanently block the Builder attempt. Restrict removal to the creation verb actually governed by the negation instead of permitting unrelated filler words before it.

codex_findings.title: Keep declared creation demands as fence errors
codex_findings.detail: When an objective both requests creation and includes the edit-only boilerplate, `creates` is true but this branch unconditionally downgrades the file-only fence to `WARN`; the new regression test even uses `Add a helper... This packet creates no new production files.` as its accepted case. Because warnings exit successfully, a contradictory packet can reach Builder and then irreparably violate scope when it creates the requested helper. Preserve `ERROR` whenever `creates` is true, and consult the declaration only when no creation demand was detected.

review_units.title: feat(kitty-chat): mount todo and monitor surfaces
review_units.head: c72e593a665f370ec414e46b6aa2a765f9c5095e

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed monitor-list responses
codex_findings.detail: Mounting this panel makes `fetchGatewayMonitors()` user-facing, but that helper still converts any successful response without a `watches` array into `[]`. If the gateway or proxy returns a malformed 2xx payload such as `{}`, the panel reports `no monitors yet` instead of entering its unavailable/retry state, hiding a contract or service failure; validate the payload as `fetchGatewayTodos()` does before exposing the panel.

codex_findings.title: Render paused monitors as paused
codex_findings.detail: When a monitor has been paused through `PATCH /monitor/{monitor_id}/enabled`, it remains in `/monitors` with `enabled: false`, but `GatewayMonitor` omits that field and this ternary still labels it `watching` unless its last keyword matched. The newly mounted Automations surface therefore tells users a disabled monitor is actively polling; preserve `enabled` in the client model and render a paused state before evaluating the match status.

codex_findings.title: Disable monitor removal while its mutation is pending
codex_findings.detail: On a slow connection, this remove button remains enabled while `removeMonitor` is pending, so a double-click sends two DELETE requests for the same ID. The first removes the monitor and the second receives the route's not-found response, leaving the mutation in an error state and showing `Couldn't remove monitor right now` even though removal succeeded; disable the control while pending or track the ID currently being removed.

codex_findings.title: Preserve failures from every clear-done deletion
codex_findings.detail: When more than one completed todo exists, `clear done` invokes `deleteTodo.mutate` once per row, but TanStack's `MutationObserver` detaches from the previous mutation on every call, so this `deleteTodo.isError` branch observes only the final deletion. If an earlier DELETE fails and the last one succeeds, the failed row reappears after invalidation while no failure message remains, making a partial clear silent; execute the deletes as one tracked batch or explicitly aggregate every rejection.

codex_findings.title: Register the Tasks surface in the workspace header
codex_findings.detail: When desktop users open Tasks, this new branch sets the active view to `tasks`, but `TopBar.tsx` has no `tasks` entry in `SURFACE_LABELS` and therefore displays its fallback label, `Kitty`; `TodoPanel` also has no heading of its own. The resulting destination is visibly mislabeled rather than identified as Tasks, so add the surface label or render a Tasks heading with the panel.

review_units.title: fix(deadlines): wire escalation delivery
review_units.head: 0a3ccfdc6b02ecd1489e8631ddce900f2fbefa75

codex_findings.title: Claim each checkpoint before concurrent delivery paths run
codex_findings.detail: When the 09:00 cron run overlaps a Home or CLI sweep, both callers can pass `escalation_already_sent()` before either sends, because the notification is delivered before `record_escalation()` performs its unique insert. The push facade's log-based dedupe has the same check-before-send race, so both executions can deliver the identical warning even though one escalation row eventually wins. Atomically claim each deadline/checkpoint before sending, with a recoverable failed state, so the newly added independent triggers cannot duplicate phone notifications.

codex_findings.title: Retry failed deliveries before advancing the schedule
codex_findings.detail: When a channel is transiently unavailable at 09:00, `claim_scheduled_run()` advances this daily schedule's `last_run` before the action executes, while `check_and_push()` leaves the failed checkpoint unrecorded. The cron therefore will not retry that occurrence, and on the following day `checkpoint_due()` no longer returns that exact checkpoint; a failed day-of notification is lost permanently, and partial failures are likewise marked completed without retry. Add bounded same-day retries or otherwise preserve failed checkpoint work instead of relying on the next daily occurrence.

codex_findings.title: Pass the user's local date into deadline checks
codex_findings.detail: When the gateway host timezone differs from the timezone configured for Kitty, this call lets `check_and_push()` use the host's `date.today()` rather than the user's date. For example, a Home sweep after UTC midnight but before midnight in America/Regina evaluates the next day's checkpoint, while the newly scheduled action is explicitly evaluated in the profile timezone by `gateway/cron.py`; this can send a warning under the wrong checkpoint or miss it in sufficiently offset timezones. Resolve the profile timezone once and pass its current date as `now` from both newly wired callers.

codex_findings.title: Distinguish quiet-hours deferral from missing setup
codex_findings.detail: When a T-7 or T-3 sweep runs during configured quiet hours, the newly restored `kind="info"` makes `push_to_jacob()` return `False` without trying any channel. This branch then labels the outcome `source_unavailable` and tells the user to check notification setup even though the actual cause is the active quiet-hours policy; the same configured channel can work immediately afterward. Preserve a distinct deferred/quiet-hours result (or at minimum give the correct recovery guidance) rather than presenting every non-delivery as broken setup.

review_units.title: feat(kitty): add live capability launcher
review_units.head: 1558774a21365c548969014fdc79db45df1b8c29

codex_findings.title: Accept every skill name the catalog can launch
codex_findings.detail: This directive parser accepts only ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens, while the existing skill importer accepts Unicode alphanumeric names through `str.isalnum()` and the capability route publishes every discovered name. For an imported skill such as `café`, selecting it composes `Use skill: café`, but this regex does not recognize the directive, so resolution falls through to fuzzy suggestion and the selected prompt is not injected. Use one shared name grammar for import, catalog publication, and directive parsing.

codex_findings.title: Surface unknown explicit skill selections
codex_findings.detail: When a capability becomes stale because its skill was removed after catalog loading, or when a user manually enters an unknown `Use skill:` name, this silently returns an empty hint and allows an ordinary completion to continue with no registered skill prompt. The request therefore appears accepted even though the selected capability was unavailable; raise or surface a clear skill-not-found error instead of silently degrading.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the selected skill's complete instructions
codex_findings.detail: For standard-tier chat turns, this prompt is subsequently placed in the existing `skill` context block, which receives only 5% of the 8,000-byte budget, while `_fit_context_blocks` gives spare capacity to earlier blocks first. With the installed skills, `agent-council` is clipped from 888 to 398 bytes, `verified-delivery` from 3,832 to 399, and `isa` from 13,718 to 399, omitting most workflow and safety instructions. Consequently, selecting these capabilities does not actually inject the installed prompt as promised; explicit skills need sufficient priority or must fail visibly when their instructions cannot fit.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the current composer draft when selecting a skill
codex_findings.detail: If the user already has an unsent draft and opens the palette through the visible toolbar button, selecting any skill replaces the entire composer value with the directive and irreversibly discards that draft. Compose the directive with the existing input, or require confirmation before replacing non-empty text, so capability selection does not cause user-data loss.

codex_findings.title: Show the capability discovery failure details
codex_findings.detail: When `/capabilities` times out, returns an HTTP error, or yields invalid JSON, `fetchCapabilities` preserves a concrete error string, but this branch discards it and shows only a fixed fallback sentence with no retry or technical details. Operators therefore cannot distinguish a stopped gateway, authorization failure, malformed response, or server error from the UI even though the evidence is available; render `capabilityError` in a bounded details/retry affordance rather than hiding the real cause.

codex_findings.title: Expose only skills this chat runtime can execute
codex_findings.detail: In the inspected kitty-chat launch flow, `streamChat` never supplies tools, so the completions route installs `_NO_TOOL_EXECUTOR_SYSTEM` and strips tool-call fields. Publishing every discovered skill nevertheless advertises capabilities such as `agent-council`, `image-gen`, and `journal-entry`, whose instructions require subprocesses, API calls, or file writes that this runtime is explicitly unable to perform. Selecting these entries can therefore only yield an unavailable-tools response or an unsupported claim; filter the catalog to skills executable in this runtime or route activation through an existing executor.

codex_findings.title: Refresh the registry before projecting live capabilities
codex_findings.detail: After the first request—or any earlier registry consumer—`skill_registry.discover()` returns its cached `_registry` unless `force_refresh=True` is supplied. Installing, removing, or editing a `SKILL.md` while the gateway remains running therefore leaves every subsequent `GET /capabilities` stale: removed skills remain advertised and new or updated skills do not appear until restart. Refresh discovery here or invalidate the registry when skills change.
