review_units.title: feat(library): add safe artifact canvas
review_units.head: 24c64a3be1b25020b60c5d36de14227ffac5ea90

codex_findings.title: Surface canvas chat rejections inside the canvas
codex_findings.detail: When `Use in chat` is clicked from the canvas and the gateway rejects the artifact—for example because the backing image was removed or grew beyond the limit after the list loaded—`handleUseInChat` writes `useError` into the Library section, but `selectedArtifact` remains set and the fixed backdrop hides that alert. The canvas therefore appears to do nothing, unlike the same action from the row; pass the error into the canvas or close it before exposing the rejection.

codex_findings.title: Preserve previews for local-path captures
codex_findings.detail: When a user captures a supported local `.md`, `.txt`, `.pdf`, or image through the path form of `/capture/file`, `post_capture_file` passes `media_type=None` (`gateway/routes/capture.py:257-260`), which ArtifactStore persists as `application/octet-stream` (`gateway/artifact_store.py:68-72`). This exact media-type gate consequently hides the Open action, and the new content endpoint would return 415, so path-captured files cannot use the canvas despite being accepted capture types. Infer or normalize their media type before applying the preview allowlist.

codex_findings.title: Move keyboard focus into the modal and contain it
codex_findings.detail: For keyboard and screen-reader users, opening the canvas leaves focus on the underlying Library Open button, and neither the page behind the `aria-modal` dialog nor its other controls are made inert. Tab and Enter can consequently continue operating hidden Library actions instead of navigating the canvas. Focus the close control or heading on mount, trap focus within the dialog, and restore it to the opener on close.

codex_findings.title: Report image preview load failures
codex_findings.detail: If a listed image disappears, becomes unreadable, or the content request is rejected after the Library query succeeds, this `` has no error handler and the canvas only shows a broken-image placeholder while retaining its actions. The backend explicitly reports these failures, but this renderer discards that evidence; handle `onError` or preflight the request so the canvas displays a clear failure reason.

codex_findings.title: Block automatic remote loads from Markdown previews
codex_findings.detail: When a captured or imported Markdown artifact contains `![alt](https://host/path)`, the default ReactMarkdown renderer emits an `` and the browser contacts that host as soon as the nominally passive preview opens. This leaks network/request metadata and can make requests to LAN services without an explicit user action, undermining the local-first boundary; provide an image component or URL transform that blocks external resources or requires consent.

codex_findings.title: Preserve byte-range headers for inline PDFs
codex_findings.detail: The PDF is loaded through the shared Next proxy, but the inspected proxy handler forwards only `Content-Type` upstream and returns only `Content-Type` plus Kitty headers, dropping `Range`/`If-Range` and `Accept-Ranges`/`Content-Range`. Starlette's `FileResponse` range support therefore never reaches the browser, so an inline PDF—up to the 50 MiB capture limit—must be transferred in full instead of supporting incremental loading and seeking. Extend the proxy's request and response header allowlists for artifact content.

codex_findings.title: Reserve the mobile bottom safe area for canvas actions
codex_findings.detail: In standalone iOS mode this fullscreen canvas covers the app's safe-area-aware bottom navigation, but its footer uses fixed padding with no `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. On devices with a home indicator, the `Use in chat` and `Open raw` controls can consequently sit inside the unsafe bottom region even though the rest of the mobile UI reserves it. Add the bottom safe-area inset to the footer padding.

codex_findings.title: Make artifact IDs round-trip through the content route
codex_findings.detail: For an explicit artifact ID containing `/`, which `artifact_store.register_file` currently permits, this produces a `%2F` path segment that Starlette decodes before route matching; `/artifacts/a%2Fb/content` therefore returns 404 rather than looking up `a/b`. I reproduced that response with the FastAPI route, while the new frontend test only asserts the generated URL and thus masks the end-to-end failure. Either constrain artifact IDs at registration or use a routing/encoding scheme that preserves arbitrary supported IDs.

codex_findings.title: Add a timeout to artifact text fetches
codex_findings.detail: If the proxy or gateway accepts this request but stalls, the browser fetch has no built-in timeout, so the canvas remains on “Loading artifact…” indefinitely; closing it only suppresses the eventual state update and does not cancel the request. Use an `AbortController` with the module's existing `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` pattern so the failure becomes visible and the transfer is actually stopped.

codex_findings.title: Preserve artifact rejection details
codex_findings.detail: When a listed text artifact becomes missing, non-ready, or otherwise unpreviewable before it is opened, the content endpoint returns a specific 404/409/415 `detail`, but this branch discards the response body and throws only the status line. `describeFailure` then replaces that with generic—and for a missing artifact, misleading—copy, hiding the gateway's clear cause; parse and propagate the endpoint detail as the nearby use-in-chat flow does.

codex_findings.title: Bound text previews before materializing the response
codex_findings.detail: When a saved plain-text or Markdown artifact is large, this eagerly copies the entire response into a string and the canvas then parses the whole string into a Markdown AST/DOM. The supported capture flow permits files up to 50 MiB, and direct ArtifactStore registrations have no size cap, so opening an otherwise valid artifact can freeze or exhaust the browser tab. Reject oversized text previews, truncate them explicitly, or load them incrementally before calling `response.text()`.

codex_findings.title: Verify registered content before serving it
codex_findings.detail: If a backing file is modified after registration, this serves the current bytes without comparing them to the artifact's stored `content_hash` or `size_bytes`. The same artifact ID can therefore display content that no longer matches its immutable registry metadata, while the canvas continues showing the stale registered size and provenance. Validate the file against the registered identity or explicitly refresh the artifact before returning it.

review_units.title: docs(packets): compile verified INSTANT wave
review_units.head: edf1928b0b87ccefbf2879d288a211538f8006a5

codex_findings.title: Invalidate the composed state after primary mutations
codex_findings.detail: After these cards switch their reads to `['state', 'now']`, keeping the existing mutation hooks unchanged leaves the displayed composed data stale: action approval/rejection/execution invalidates only `['actions']`, project refresh invalidates `['projects']`, and deadline sweep invalidates `['deadlines']`. A successful primary action can therefore remain visible and actionable until the 30-second `/state/now` poll, potentially inviting a duplicate click that then fails. The refactor must invalidate or patch the composed query after each retained mutation.

codex_findings.title: Make the delayed-section smoke test achievable
codex_findings.detail: Because `/state/now` returns one non-streaming JSON document, delaying that route delays every section; the frontend cannot receive successful sibling sections while one section is still pending. With the backend deadline remaining three seconds, this also conflicts with the next step's 1500 ms useful-content requirement. Test an immediate per-section `ok: false` response instead, lower the backend deadline below the paint budget, or introduce a transport that can deliver sections independently.

codex_findings.title: Record an observed RED gate for the frontend packets
codex_findings.detail: This paragraph explicitly substitutes source inspection for an observed failing test, even though Packet Standard §8 requires the Tier 1 gate to fail before the change and record its current output; `KF-GLANCE-02.md:35` makes the same substitution. Without running a temporary characterization, the planned assertions may pass vacuously or fail for unrelated setup, so add the tests temporarily, run the exact Vitest commands, record the failing assertions, and then restore the planning-only tree as KF-GLANCE-01 does.

codex_findings.title: Avoid scheduling refresh exactly at the cache TTL
codex_findings.detail: When a warm run starts at time T, cron records `last_run=T` before executing, but the cache entry expires 300 seconds after `unified_context()` finishes at T+d. The next five-minute run therefore commonly arrives at T+300 while the entry is still valid, skips it, and leaves the cache cold from T+d+300 until roughly T+600. The cadence or skip logic must account for remaining TTL rather than scheduling exactly at the TTL boundary.

review_units.title: feat(kitty): add live activity center
review_units.head: 3a3cb4ef720708793aa065b4a6a5a6467cf3ef15

codex_findings.title: Prioritize failed activity ahead of running work
codex_findings.detail: When the combined collectors yield at least `limit` waiting/running items, assigning `failed` a lower priority than `running` causes every later failure to be sliced away at line 157. The returned counts then report zero failures and the top-bar attention badge omits them even though the sources supplied real failure evidence. Rank failed items with the attention states before running work, or reserve space and compute attention counts before truncating.

codex_findings.title: Limit partial degradation to expected source failures
codex_findings.detail: If any collector has a programming or data-shape error, this catch-all converts it into a successful HTTP 200 with an empty source and only a truncated exception string. That hides defects such as the Builder timestamp failure from normal error handling and monitoring instead of raising the real error with its context; catch only known availability exceptions here and allow unexpected exceptions to fail the request loudly.

codex_findings.title: Fetch unresolved actions before applying the history limit
codex_findings.detail: When more than 30 action records exist, this query selects the newest IDs before normalization, regardless of status. An older `proposed`, `approved`, `executing`, or `failed` action therefore disappears once 30 newer actions are recorded; for example, 30 later rejected actions make a still-pending approval vanish from both the Activity list and its attention count. Query unresolved statuses separately or apply the limit only after state-aware prioritization.

codex_findings.title: Surface approved actions as stalled rather than running
codex_findings.detail: When approval succeeds but the subsequent `/execute` request fails before the gateway claims the row, the durable action remains `approved`; `HomeState` explicitly notes that such an action can sit approved forever. Mapping it to `running` removes it from the attention badge and presents it as active work even though no executor is running and user intervention is required, so classify this stranded state as actionable and provide a retry path.

codex_findings.title: Fetch failed automations before limiting recent history
codex_findings.detail: When an automation failure is followed by 30 newer runs, `list_runs(limit=30)` excludes that unresolved failure before the activity projection can prioritize it. The “Needs repair” group and top-bar attention count then report no failure even though durable failure evidence remains; query failure/running statuses separately or apply the history limit after state-aware prioritization.

codex_findings.title: Map the action queue's actual unknown status to failed
codex_findings.detail: After a gateway restart interrupts an executing action, `action_queue.reconcile_stale_executing()` persists the status as `unknown`, not `outcome_unknown`. Consequently this mapping misses precisely the ambiguous-side-effect case and the fallback at line 48 presents it as `running` instead of under “Needs repair,” potentially leaving the user waiting rather than reconciling an unknown external outcome. Map `unknown` explicitly and include the stored result explaining why review is required.

codex_findings.title: Fetch unresolved agents before limiting recent history
codex_findings.detail: When a failed, interrupted, or still-active agent is older than 30 newer sessions, `list_agents(limit=30)` excludes it before the projection can prioritize states; `agent_runner.list_agents()` orders solely by `created_at DESC`. The unresolved session then disappears from the Activity list and attention count even though its durable record remains, so unresolved statuses must be fetched separately or the limit applied after state-aware prioritization.

codex_findings.title: Route action activity to a surface that displays it
codex_findings.detail: For any non-`proposed` action—especially a failed action under “Needs repair”—the Open button navigates to Home, but both Home action consumers call `useActions('proposed')`; repo-wide search finds no other UI consumer that renders approved, failed, or completed actions. The selected activity therefore disappears as soon as the panel closes, leaving no way to inspect or repair it; deep-link to an action history/detail surface or make Home render the targeted record.

codex_findings.title: Treat user-cancelled agents as completed
codex_findings.detail: When a user deliberately stops an agent, `agent_runner.stop()` persists the terminal status `cancelled`, but this branch classifies it as a failure. Every intentional cancellation consequently appears under “Needs repair” and increments the global attention badge despite requiring no repair; keep `failed` and `interrupted` in the failure group, but classify operator cancellation as completed.

codex_findings.title: Route agent activity to its owning session UI
codex_findings.detail: For every item collected from `agent_runner.list_agents()`, this destination opens the `agents` view, but `ViewRenderer` renders `AgentWorkspacePanel` there, which reads the separate shared-workspace ledger rather than `autonomy_sessions`; the selected `source_id` is not passed through, and repo-wide search finds no UI consumer of `useAgentSessions`. Consequently, opening a running or failed agent activity shows an unrelated room and provides no way to inspect that session, so these rows need a destination that renders the owning agent-session record.

codex_findings.title: Open the owning automation run
codex_findings.detail: For an automation failure, this destination only opens the generic Automations view while `page.tsx` ignores `source_id` for every source except agents. `AutomationsView` renders schedules, routines, and monitors, and `CronPanel` can inspect only a schedule's latest run—not this run ID—so an older failed/interrupted run (or one followed by a success) disappears after the user clicks Open and cannot be inspected or retried. Pass the run/schedule identity through navigation and select a surface that renders that exact run.

codex_findings.title: Exclude superseded Builder initiatives from Needs you
codex_findings.detail: When an active initiative is superseded, Builder deliberately preserves it by setting `state='paused'` together with `superseded_by`; however, `build_control_plane_summary()` drops the supersession fields, and this mapping consequently presents historical superseded work as “Needs you” forever and inflates the global attention count. Carry the durable supersession marker through the supported Builder projection and classify or exclude those historical initiatives rather than treating every pause as actionable.

codex_findings.title: Parse Builder timestamps before converting them
codex_findings.detail: Whenever the Builder database contains an initiative, `build_control_plane_summary()` supplies its SQLite `TIMESTAMP` as a string such as `2026-08-31 18:00:00`; calling `float()` here raises `ValueError`. The surrounding source wrapper then marks Builder unavailable and omits every Builder initiative, so a core Activity source is broken in normal populated installations. Parse the timestamp explicitly (or preserve a sortable timestamp representation) and test with the real summary shape rather than a numeric mock.

codex_findings.title: Distinguish queued Builder initiatives from running work
codex_findings.detail: When an initiative is merely active with queued eligible packets, the supported Builder summary reports `state='active'` even though no lease, worker, or run exists; the existing Builder status test demonstrates this exact `queue.queued=1` shape. Falling through here maps that initiative to `running`, so Activity claims it is “In motion” while Builder may be completely idle. Derive this state from Builder's packet/run projection (and supervisor truth where needed) rather than treating the initiative execution gate as evidence of execution.

codex_findings.title: Preserve unknown attention counts during partial degradation
codex_findings.detail: When `/activity` returns its designed partial response with one source marked unavailable, the missing source contributes no items, yet this calculation turns the partial `waiting` and `failed` totals into an exact-looking count. If Actions is unavailable while other sources are quiet, the global button shows no badge and says only “Open activity,” concealing that approvals could not be counted; propagate a degraded/unknown state to the TopBar instead of presenting the partial count as complete.

codex_findings.title: Fetch unresolved action statuses before filtering
codex_findings.detail: When 50 newer terminal actions exist, `useActions()` receives only those rows because `/actions` applies its default history limit before this client-side filter. An older `approved`, `failed`, `unknown`, or `outcome_unknown` action can therefore appear in Activity but disappear after Open navigates to Home, leaving no visible run/review path. Query each unresolved status directly or add a server-side unresolved-status query rather than filtering bounded history.

codex_findings.title: Move keyboard focus into the activity dialog
codex_findings.detail: When a keyboard user opens Activity from the TopBar, focus remains on the now-obscured Activity button because opening the dialog only installs an Escape listener. Pressing Tab then advances through the underlying toolbar controls instead of the close button or activity rows, despite the panel declaring `aria-modal="true"`. Focus an element inside the panel on open and keep background controls inert or trap focus until the dialog closes.

codex_findings.title: Show refresh failures when cached activity exists
codex_findings.detail: After one successful query, a later polling failure leaves React Query's cached `projection` populated while setting `error`; this condition therefore suppresses the error and continues displaying stale counts and work as though they were current. The failure only appears on the initial load, so gateway outages after startup become invisible in the Activity Center. Render a stale/unavailable warning whenever `error` is present, while optionally retaining the cached rows.

codex_findings.title: Translate source failures before rendering them
codex_findings.detail: When Builder has not been initialized, `build_control_plane_summary()` raises a `FileNotFoundError` containing the resolved Builder database path, and this line renders that raw reason directly (for example, `builder: Builder queue database does not exist: /Users/.../builder_queue.db`). The global Activity panel therefore exposes internal filesystem paths as primary product copy on otherwise normal installations; show plain recovery-oriented source copy here and keep the diagnostic detail in logs or a secondary disclosure.

review_units.title: feat(projects): add resumable project workspace
review_units.head: fa330c927122660a6375570bb6ce06154d731c8c

codex_findings.title: Preserve the partial refresh error details
codex_findings.detail: When `/refresh` returns HTTP 200 with `next_step.ok === false`, the payload includes the actual failure in `next_step.error`, but this branch replaces it with a generic retry message. Fresh evidence in the reviewed SHA is that the newly added partial-failure branch still discards that response context, leaving users unable to distinguish model availability, configuration, or other generation failures; include the returned error in the alert.

codex_findings.title: Surface next-step query failures in the workspace
codex_findings.detail: When the bulk `useProjectNextSteps` request rejects, this converts its missing data to `null` without forwarding `isError`; opening the workspace therefore reports “No generated next step yet” even though the step is unavailable rather than absent. Pass the pending/error state through and render the same explicit failure shown by the project card.

codex_findings.title: Report degraded refresh sources in the workspace
codex_findings.detail: When the git, memory, or signals source times out or throws, `project_resume.refresh` deliberately returns HTTP 200 with `sources[name].ok === false`, but this logic checks only a rejected mutation and `next_step.ok`. The workspace therefore drops the source errors and presents an incomplete refreshed summary as a successful refresh; extend the refresh response type and surface each degraded source with its returned context.

codex_findings.title: Derive workspace content from live query state
codex_findings.detail: When the project list finishes before the batched next-step query, opening the workspace captures `null` here and continues showing “No generated next step yet” even after that query completes. The same stale snapshot means a successful Refresh cannot update the workspace’s summary, open actions, or next step because subsequent query results update the parent variables but not this state object. Store the selected project ID and derive the current project and next step on every render instead.

codex_findings.title: Handle partial next-step refresh failures
codex_findings.detail: When the project data refresh succeeds but next-step generation fails, `gateway/routes/projects.py::post_refresh` intentionally returns HTTP 200 with `next_step: { ok: false, error: ... }`; this callback discards that successful mutation payload, so the workspace stops showing “refreshing…” while retaining the old or empty step and provides no indication that generation failed. Inspect `next_step.ok` and surface its error instead of treating every resolved request as a complete refresh.

codex_findings.title: Suspend the workspace focus trap for the command palette
codex_findings.detail: When Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the now-visible command palette above the workspace, this focus trap remains enabled because it only accounts for `selectedArtifact`. On the next Tab, `useDialogFocus` sees focus outside its section and moves it back into the workspace; Escape is also handled by both document listeners and can close the workspace along with the palette. Fresh evidence in this head is that the stacking fix changed only z-index ordering, leaving the workspace trap active while the palette is open.

codex_findings.title: Move keyboard focus into the workspace dialog
codex_findings.detail: When a keyboard user opens the workspace, focus remains on the underlying “Open workspace” trigger because the dialog neither focuses one of its controls nor traps focus. Since the project list remains mounted before the dialog in DOM order, subsequent Tab presses reach hidden Refresh and Project context controls behind the backdrop, allowing the user to operate the obscured page despite `aria-modal="true"`; focus the dialog on mount, contain Tab navigation, and restore focus when it closes.

codex_findings.title: Sanitize the project summary before rendering it
codex_findings.detail: When a code project has been refreshed, `gateway/project_resume.py::_render_summary` can store internal text such as `main (dirty); 4 memory mention(s)` or path-registration instructions. The project list intentionally passes this field through `projectSummaryCopy`, but the workspace header renders `project.summary` directly, exposing the internal copy again; apply the same summary sanitizer here.

codex_findings.title: Prevent canceled activation from re-scoping the current chat
codex_findings.detail: When project activation is slow and the user dismisses the workspace before this await resolves, the guard returns only after `mutateAsync` has persisted the new active project and updated the shared cache, while also skipping `onStartChat`. If the user later opens Chat and sends from their existing project-A conversation, the request carries project B and `chat_lifecycle.start_turn` silently reassigns that conversation to B. Fresh evidence in this head is that the cancellation guard suppresses only navigation and fresh-chat creation, not the completed activation; prevent dismissal while pending, roll the activation back, or otherwise ensure the old chat cannot be reused.

codex_findings.title: Cancel navigation after the workspace closes
codex_findings.detail: When the active-project request is slow, the user can dismiss the workspace with its close button, backdrop, or Escape while this await is pending. The promise survives the unmount and then calls `onNavigate(view)` unconditionally, pulling the user into Chat or Work after they canceled the interaction; guard the continuation with a mounted/request token or prevent dismissal while activation is pending.

codex_findings.title: Apply the project copy sanitizer in the workspace
codex_findings.detail: For code or incompletely configured projects whose generated step contains text such as `git status`, dirty branches, repository details, or path-registration instructions, this renders the raw internal text. The existing project list and Home surfaces deliberately call `projectNextStepCopy` to replace exactly this content with user-facing copy, so opening the new workspace re-exposes wording those surfaces suppress; sanitize the step, reason, and recent win before rendering them here.

codex_findings.title: Start a project-scoped chat before continuing
codex_findings.detail: When the user already has a conversation associated with project A, opens project B's workspace, clicks Continue in chat, and sends a message, this only changes the active project and view while retaining the existing active chat. `KittyContext.runStream` then submits that chat's ID with project B's ID, and `chat_lifecycle.start_turn` updates the conversation row to the supplied project, silently moving the entire conversation from A's Project Resume history to B; create or select a B-scoped conversation before navigating instead of reusing an arbitrary active chat.

codex_findings.title: Surface failures from workspace refreshes
codex_findings.detail: If the project refresh request rejects, `useRefreshProject().mutate` retains the error internally, but the workspace receives only the pending flag and renders no failure state; the spinner simply returns to “Refresh,” making the failed external operation indistinguishable from success. Pass and display the mutation error with useful request/response context rather than silently discarding it.

codex_findings.title: Surface degraded Builder source state in Project Resume
codex_findings.detail: When `build_status_snapshot` fails or reports partial integrity, the resume payload's `work.source` is explicitly `degraded` with a reason, but `GatewayProjectWork` omits that field and this branch renders the remaining items—or no section at all—as normal. Preserve and display the source state just as the workspace already does for conversation and deadline failures, so missing or partial Builder work is not mistaken for a complete result.

codex_findings.title: Keep the command palette above the workspace
codex_findings.detail: When the workspace is open and the user presses Cmd/Ctrl+K, the globally mounted `CommandPalette` opens and autofocuses its input, but its backdrop uses `zIndex: 1000`, below this new `zIndex: 1225` backdrop. The palette is therefore completely hidden behind the workspace while stealing keyboard focus, making the shortcut unusable until the workspace is dismissed; align the overlay stacking order so the active palette is visible.

codex_findings.title: Keep the command palette above artifact previews
codex_findings.detail: When an artifact preview is open and the user presses Cmd/Ctrl+K, this newly reachable `ArtifactCanvas` remains at z-index 1200 while `CommandPalette` is at 1000, so the palette opens invisibly behind the preview and autofocuses its hidden input. Fresh evidence in the current head is that the workspace backdrop was lowered below the palette, but the nested artifact mounted here was not; either suppress the shortcut while this modal is active or place the palette above the entire modal stack.

codex_findings.title: Hide the parent dialog while previewing an artifact
codex_findings.detail: When a user opens a previewable artifact, this mounts `ArtifactCanvas` as a second `aria-modal` dialog while the project workspace remains an active `aria-modal` dialog underneath it. The focus hook disables the workspace's keyboard trap, but assistive-technology virtual navigation can still reach and operate the workspace controls behind the artifact; mark the parent dialog inert/hidden while `selectedArtifact` is set so only the top modal is exposed.

review_units.title: feat(chat): render live action objects
review_units.head: 9a7053796ddd5af0d2a5932484a8ba9b4f523d01

codex_findings.title: Preserve the exact durable artifact ID
codex_findings.detail: When an artifact is registered with a nonblank ID containing leading or trailing whitespace, `artifact_store.register_file()` accepts and stores that ID unchanged, and the inventory emits it unchanged, but this trim makes the card request a different row. The reference therefore reports the artifact unavailable or, if the trimmed ID also exists, opens the wrong artifact; use `trim()` only to validate that the parsed ID is nonblank and pass the original string through, or normalize IDs consistently at the storage boundary.

codex_findings.title: Restrict live action fences to assistant messages
codex_findings.detail: Because this `CodeBlock` renderer is shared by user and assistant messages and never checks the supplied `isUser` value, a user who pastes or discusses a `kitty-action` fence gets a live `ActionCard` rather than quoted code. If the numeric ID exists, that card exposes its payload and mutation controls, turning ordinary user-authored text into an unrelated Approve/Run/Reject surface; gate typed-object rendering by message role.

codex_findings.title: Add a producer for typed chat references
codex_findings.detail: A repo-wide search for `kitty-action` and `kitty-artifact` finds only these rendering branches and their hard-coded tests; no system prompt, response builder, or action/artifact workflow emits either fence. Consequently ordinary Chat responses never contain the syntax needed to reach these cards, so the advertised feature is limited to manually authored or imported messages; wire durable IDs into the chat response path and add an end-to-end test that exercises that producer.

codex_findings.title: Derive action controls from the current policy
codex_findings.detail: When a durable proposal survives a signed tier escalation, the stored row deliberately retains its old `risk_tier` while `action_queue.execute()` enforces the current registry tier. For example, the repository's escalation test creates a row stamped T0 and then changes the live tier to T2; this card still displays T0, offers only Run, and provides no Approve control even though the backend now requires approval. Return the effective tier or policy decision from the authoritative read and derive these controls from that instead of the stale proposal field.

codex_findings.title: Use the grant decision to choose action controls
codex_findings.detail: When a proposed T0/T1 action is covered by a matching `ask` grant, these tier-only predicates render Run and omit Approve; checked `action_queue.execute()`, which calls `action_grants.evaluate()` and returns 403 until that proposal becomes approved, leaving this card unable to perform the required one-shot approval. A matching `deny` grant likewise still presents Run. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier tier-escalation report is the scoped-grant contract in `tests/test_action_grants.py`, where `ask` blocks a proposed action but permits it after approval; return the effective policy outcome from `GET /actions/{id}` and derive the controls from that decision rather than the registry tier alone.

codex_findings.title: Hide Run while the action is already executing
codex_findings.detail: When polling reads an action in `executing`, policy evaluation can still report `allow` for T0/T1, and this predicate does not restrict Run to `proposed` or `approved`. A refreshed card—or another card for the same long-running action—therefore presents an enabled Run button alongside “Running…”, although `action_queue.execute()` rejects that status with 409. Require an executable lifecycle status before setting `canRun`.

codex_findings.title: Clear obsolete mutation errors after a successful action
codex_findings.detail: If one mutation fails and a different mutation later succeeds—for example, Run loses a policy race, polling exposes Approve, and approval succeeds—the first hook's `error` remains set. Aggregating all three persistent errors here consequently keeps rendering “Action did not change” even after the authoritative row reflects the successful operation, including on terminal states such as rejected. Reset the other mutation states on a new attempt/success or associate the displayed error with the current operation.

codex_findings.title: Surface failed action mutations
codex_findings.detail: When `/approve`, `/reject`, or `/execute` returns a 4xx/5xx response—for example after a concurrent decision, tier change, or expired grant—the mutation enters its error state, but this card never renders any of the three mutation errors. The unchanged controls therefore make the operation appear to have been ignored and hide the server's reason; render `describeFailure` for the failed mutation so the user can tell that approval or execution did not occur.

codex_findings.title: Keep Reject available for every proposed action
codex_findings.detail: For proposed T0/T1 actions, `canApprove` is false, so nesting Reject inside this branch leaves Run as the card's only control. The backend explicitly permits `proposed → rejected` for every tier, and these actions include local mutations such as `todo.create` and `note.draft`; users viewing one in Chat therefore cannot decline it without navigating to another surface. Render Reject whenever the action is still proposed, independently of whether approval is required.

codex_findings.title: Recognize the backend's unknown execution outcome
codex_findings.detail: After a gateway restart interrupts an executing action, `action_queue.reconcile_stale_executing()` emits the terminal status `unknown` because the external side effect may or may not have happened. This component checks only the nonexistent status `outcome_unknown`, so that safety-critical ambiguous result is rendered with the ordinary neutral status color rather than the destructive treatment intended here; use `unknown` consistently in both the terminal and status-style checks.

codex_findings.title: Show the recorded artifact failure reason
codex_findings.detail: When a durable artifact has `state: "failed"` and a populated `error`, the metadata request succeeds, so the earlier query-error branch is skipped and this generic message hides the recorded cause. The artifact schema explicitly supports failed rows, and the existing Library surface renders `artifact.error`; show that same error here (with alert semantics) so a failed report or file does not appear merely unpreviewable.

codex_findings.title: Stop polling terminal action rows
codex_findings.detail: For every mounted action card, this interval continues issuing a GET every five seconds even after the row reaches the immutable `executed`, `failed`, or `rejected` state. A visible chat containing historical action cards consequently generates 720 requests per card per hour without any possible state change; make the interval conditional on the returned status and disable it for terminal rows.

codex_findings.title: Do not match project actions by a non-unique name
codex_findings.detail: When two projects share a name, which the projects schema and create route permit, adding that name to `project_scope_ids` makes the scoped query select every action whose `scope_type` is `project` and whose `scope_id` equals the shared name. A chat in one project can therefore receive the durable ID, payload, and mutation controls for an action intended for the other project. Match on the stable numeric project ID, or resolve legacy name-scoped rows only when the name identifies exactly one project.

codex_findings.title: Filter scoped actions before applying the global cap
codex_findings.detail: `list_actions(limit=50)` applies its descending global limit before this loop checks conversation or project ownership. Once 50 unrelated newer actions exist, an older pending action for the current chat or project is never considered, so the model receives no reference even though the authoritative scoped action still exists; perform the scope filtering in the store query and then apply the six-object presentation limit.

codex_findings.title: Do not hide durable inventory failures
codex_findings.detail: When either inventory read raises—for example because the action tier registry is invalid or artifact metadata is corrupt—this broad handler logs and returns an empty block, allowing the chat to continue as though no durable objects exist. That hides unavailable authoritative evidence from both the model and user; propagate the failure or expose an explicit degraded state instead.

codex_findings.title: Treat durable object labels as untrusted prompt data
codex_findings.detail: Artifact display names originate from captured local paths or multipart filenames, but `_one_line` only collapses whitespace before inserting the value directly into this system message; action titles are handled the same way above. A file named with instruction-like text therefore becomes higher-priority model input on every scoped chat turn, and can redirect the answer or tool-capable caller despite being metadata. Delimit and explicitly label these fields as untrusted data, or use a structured representation that cannot be mistaken for instructions.

codex_findings.title: Keep optional inventory outside required safety context
codex_findings.detail: When a long current turn leaves enough context budget for the existing no-tool safety prompt but not for that prompt plus the durable-object inventory, appending the inventory here makes the entire combined `tool_system` required. `_fit_final_model_messages()` then returns 413 rather than omitting the optional card inventory, so requests that previously fit fail whenever scoped objects happen to exist. Budget the inventory separately from the required safety text or drop it when it cannot fit.

review_units.title: feat(chat): add durable @ context mentions
review_units.head: 580fef4c69b5fa799e2cccb67cc731def6258529

codex_findings.title: Leave marker-free message formatting unchanged
codex_findings.detail: `_prepare_explicit_context` runs `strip_context_markers` over every model-visible message, but this function calls `.strip()` and collapses every run of three or more newlines even when the text contains no context marker. As a result, ordinary API callers lose leading indentation and all conversations have intentional blank lines rewritten before dispatch, which can alter whitespace-sensitive pasted code or structured text; return the original string byte-for-byte when no marker was removed and only normalize whitespace created by marker removal.

codex_findings.title: Let unexpected context-store failures abort the request
codex_findings.detail: When a selected object's store read or artifact file read fails because of SQLite corruption, permissions, or another operational error, this broad catch converts the exception into a warning and continues without the context the user explicitly selected. These warnings are only appended to `bundle.warnings` and are neither returned nor logged, so the response silently proceeds with incomplete primary context; only expected stale-object failures should degrade, while unexpected failures should be raised visibly.

codex_findings.title: Bound artifact reads before loading the file
codex_findings.detail: For a large ready text artifact, `Path.read_text()` loads and decodes the entire file before the 8,000-character slice is applied. Captured artifacts can be tens of megabytes and internally registered artifacts have no store-level size cap, so selecting one can allocate the whole file and block the async completions route despite the advertised bounded context; open the file and read only the required prefix.

codex_findings.title: Reject undecodable selected text artifacts
codex_findings.detail: When a ready text artifact contains invalid UTF-8, `errors="replace"` silently substitutes replacement characters and injects corrupted evidence as the user-selected primary context. Because this path reports neither an error nor a warning, the model can answer from altered content while the user believes the original artifact was used; decode strictly and surface the resulting artifact error instead.

codex_findings.title: Verify artifact integrity before injecting its content
codex_findings.detail: This reads the backing path without comparing its current size and SHA-256 hash to the immutable `size_bytes` and `content_hash` recorded at registration. If a registered source file is edited, replaced, or corrupted afterward, selecting the artifact injects the changed bytes under the old durable ID and provenance, whereas the existing artifact preview path correctly rejects this condition and requires refresh or re-import; apply the same integrity check before using the file as model context.

codex_findings.title: Keep referenced artifact content out of system instructions
codex_findings.detail: When a selected text or Markdown artifact contains prompt-injection text, this raw content is copied into `explicit_context_block` and then appended to the system message in `gateway/routes/completions.py:589`, giving document instructions system-level authority instead of treating them as quoted data. This can override the user's actual request and, for API callers that provide tool schemas, induce attacker-directed tool calls for the caller to execute; place referenced content in a lower-trust message or add a clear untrusted-data boundary that prevents its instructions from being followed.

codex_findings.title: Read referenced chats from the durable lifecycle ledger
codex_findings.detail: When the legacy chat-blob save fails or a page reload occurs before its fire-and-forget save completes, the normalized lifecycle ledger still contains the turn and `/chats/{id}/messages` restores it in the UI. Selecting that visibly recovered conversation then calls `chats_store.get_chat()` here, so the injected context comes from the stale blob and omits the recovered messages the user selected; resolve message history from the same lifecycle projection used by chat recovery, with the blob only as the no-ledger fallback.

codex_findings.title: Preserve newest messages when clipping referenced chats
codex_findings.detail: For a referenced conversation, the last eight messages are traversed oldest-to-newest and each message consumes the remaining 6,000-character allowance from its beginning. If the earliest message in that window is at least 6,000 characters, every later message—including the most recent assistant conclusion—is omitted, so the injected context can misrepresent where the referenced chat ended; allocate the budget from the newest messages before restoring chronological order.

codex_findings.title: Refresh artifact candidates after direct uploads
codex_findings.detail: This query has no polling interval, and its 30-second `staleTime` does not itself trigger a refetch. Composer uploads in `KittyContext.handleAddFiles` call `uploadCaptureFile` directly rather than the mutation that invalidates `['artifacts']`, so an artifact created after this page-mounted query loaded remains absent from `@` suggestions until an unrelated remount or eligible focus refetch; invalidate or update this query whenever direct capture succeeds.

codex_findings.title: Surface artifact lookup failures in the context picker
codex_findings.detail: When the initial artifacts query fails because the gateway or artifact store is unavailable, this fallback silently turns the failure into an empty artifact candidate list while project and chat suggestions continue to work. The user therefore sees no artifact results and no indication that evidence is unavailable; expose `artifacts.error` in the picker/status surface instead of presenting the failure as “no artifacts.”

codex_findings.title: Select the newest prior chats for mention search
codex_findings.detail: After persisted chats load, `KittyContext` sorts them by `updatedAt` descending, so with more than 20 prior chats this `slice(-20)` retains the 20 oldest conversations rather than the most recent ones. Consequently a user cannot find or mention any recently used conversation outside the active chat; take the leading 20 entries before applying any desired display ordering.

codex_findings.title: Encode chat IDs before writing context markers
codex_findings.detail: For a persisted chat whose ID contains whitespace, such as `planning notes`, this emits `<!-- kitty-context:chat:planning notes -->`, but the gateway parser accepts only `[^^\s>]`-style IDs and consequently leaves the marker unresolved and model-visible. The `/chats` upsert path accepts any nonempty ID, including this form, so selecting such a prior chat produces a visible chip but injects none of its context; encode the ID or use a marker format that round-trips arbitrary accepted chat IDs.

codex_findings.title: Strip markers before consolidating sessions into memory
codex_findings.detail: When a session containing a short mentioned prompt is posted to `/sessions/close`, these appended markers remain in the message content, and `close_session` passes them untouched to `consolidate_session`, which copies the first 120 characters of each user message into long-term session memory. A prompt such as `Summarize @report` therefore stores internal context IDs and marker syntax that can later be retrieved into unrelated turns; strip the protocol markers at the consolidation boundary while retaining them in durable chat history.

codex_findings.title: Clear context refs when closing the active chat
codex_findings.detail: Context refs are cleared when a user explicitly selects another chat, but closing the active chat changes `activeChatId` through `handleCloseChat` without performing this reset. If the user has selected context chips and then closes that conversation, those refs remain attached to the composer for the newly activated chat and are silently persisted with its next message; apply the same reset to every active-chat transition.

codex_findings.title: Restore the bounded durable-object prompt limit
codex_findings.detail: Changing this limit from 6 to 50 lets `_durable_chat_object_system` include as many as 50 actions plus 50 artifacts on every turn. `_fit_final_model_messages` budgets this optional system block before older conversation history, so chats or projects with many durable objects can now consume the 3,000–16,000-byte tier envelope and discard substantially more prior messages even when none of those objects is relevant to the request; retain the previous small cap or select only relevant objects.

codex_findings.title: Restrict protocol-marker stripping to user messages
codex_findings.detail: This comprehension strips marker-shaped lines from every role, although durable context markers are only appended to user messages. If an API caller supplies a system instruction or an assistant response that legitimately contains an example such as `<!-- kitty-context:project:7 -->`, that content disappears before the next model request even though it was never protocol metadata; preserve non-user message content and strip markers only from user turns.

codex_findings.title: Prioritize explicit context before clipping the bundle
codex_findings.detail: When the assembled context plus runtime and safety prompts approach the tier cap, `_fit_final_model_messages` keeps only a prefix of `bundle_system`; because the selected object's block is appended at the end here, it is the first part discarded. For example, a short “summarize @report” request classified as trivial can lose the entire artifact block while still producing an answer, even though that object was selected as primary context; fit explicit context as its own higher-priority part rather than appending it behind ambient context.

review_units.title: feat(home): surface selective personal intelligence
review_units.head: 7476f449f59fffc8b0e4b9f209b88facde04e91f

codex_findings.title: Reject unresolved explicit context
codex_findings.detail: When a selected project/chat has been deleted or a text artifact's backing file is missing, this catch converts the resolution failure into a warning and the completion continues after stripping the durable marker. Those warnings are only appended to `bundle.warnings`, which is neither returned to the chat client nor logged here, so the user receives a normal-looking answer that silently omitted explicitly selected context. Raise a clear request error or surface the failure to the client instead.

codex_findings.title: Bound artifact reads before loading the file
codex_findings.detail: When a user references a large text artifact, `read_text()` decodes the entire backing file before the 8,000-character slice is applied. Captured files may be as large as 50 MiB, and one request may resolve eight references, so this async completion handler can synchronously read and allocate hundreds of megabytes while blocking the event loop even though almost all of that content is discarded. Read only a bounded prefix from the file handle before decoding.

codex_findings.title: Treat referenced artifact content as untrusted data
codex_findings.detail: When a selected uploaded text or Markdown artifact contains embedded instructions, this raw content is concatenated into `bundle_system`, placing it in the same system message as Gateway instructions under a directive to use it as primary context. An indirect prompt injection in a document being summarized can therefore steer the model—and, for callers that supply and execute tools, potentially induce unintended tool calls. Delimit the content as untrusted quoted data and explicitly prohibit following instructions found inside it, or keep it at user-message authority.

codex_findings.title: Read the persisted insight summary
codex_findings.detail: For every real item returned by `insight_loop.list_due()`, the saved text is stored in `payload["summary"]`, not `payload["text"]` (`capture()` and the existing insight-loop tests establish that schema). Consequently all returned-thought notices use the generic fallback, and the Chat prompt also omits the thought the user intended to revisit. Read `summary` here and update the projection test to use the production payload shape.

codex_findings.title: Refresh cached life suggestions before surfacing them as today
codex_findings.detail: When the gateway remains running after the first intelligence request, `morning_proactive()` returns its module-level `_PROACTIVE_CACHE` indefinitely unless the separate cache-invalidation endpoint is explicitly called, and there is no automatic invalidation caller in the gateway. The one-minute intelligence polling therefore keeps showing passed meetings, obsolete project steps, and even the previous day's suggestions under the `today` label. Use date/age-aware invalidation or a fresh life projection before adding these candidates.

codex_findings.title: Preserve deadline due-date order when ranking ties
codex_findings.detail: When more than three deadlines need confirmation, `list_needs_jacob()` supplies them in ascending `due_date` order, but assigning every deadline score 100 and then sorting ties by the string ID discards that order. A later deadline with a small ID can occupy the limited projection while an imminent deadline with a larger ID is omitted. Include `due_date` in the deadline ranking key or preserve the source order for equal-priority deadline candidates.

codex_findings.title: Surface artifact context-candidate loading failures
codex_findings.detail: When `/artifacts` fails while the user is composing a chat, this query enters an error state but the page reads only `artifacts.data ?? []`, making every artifact silently disappear from the `@` picker. There is no error passed to `InputBar` or the chat status surface, so the behavior is indistinguishable from having no saved artifacts. Render the query failure near the picker or expose it through the existing status UI.

codex_findings.title: Exclude artifacts whose contents cannot be resolved
codex_findings.detail: When the artifact list contains a PDF, image, or any non-ready/non-text artifact, this unfiltered mapping offers it in the `@` picker even though `_artifact_block` only reads ready plain-text or Markdown files. Selecting such an item sends the model only its name, media type, and state—not its contents—so requests such as summarizing a PDF or describing an image appear to use the chosen artifact but cannot do so. Filter candidates to resolvable artifacts or add an appropriate content/modality resolver and show unsupported cases explicitly.

codex_findings.title: Select the most recent conversations for context
codex_findings.detail: When more than 20 saved conversations exist, `KittyProvider` has already sorted `k.chats` by descending `updatedAt`, so `slice(-20)` selects the oldest 20 conversations rather than the most recent 20. As a result, recently updated non-active conversations disappear from the context picker for established users. Take the leading 20 entries before applying any desired display-order reversal.

codex_findings.title: Open the owning project rather than the generic project list
codex_findings.detail: When a notice has a `project_id`, this handler changes the global active-project scope and then navigates to `ProjectsView`, but that view does not consume the active project and `ProjectsPanel` initializes with no workspace selected. The user therefore lands on the full project list instead of the owning project's workspace, despite the action being labeled as opening that project. Pass the project ID as navigation state and initialize the corresponding workspace directly.

codex_findings.title: Keep connection discovery available in the empty state
codex_findings.detail: When there are active projects but no deadlines, due insights, life suggestions, or cached Magic result, this return removes the only “find connections” control. That leaves users unable to trigger the explicit generation path precisely when the cache is empty; render an empty shell with the discovery action instead of hiding the component entirely.

codex_findings.title: Show intelligence failures instead of returning nothing
codex_findings.detail: When the `/intelligence` query fails, or when every collector reports unavailable before producing an item, `projection` is absent or has an empty `items` array and this early return hides both the query failure and all source-unavailability reasons. Home therefore presents an indistinguishable normal empty state instead of the clear cause required by the repository contract; pass the query error through and render an alert or degraded shell even when there are no notices.

codex_findings.title: Display connection refresh failures
codex_findings.detail: When the explicit refresh POST fails—for example because Magic Kitty's LLM call or project-resume collection raises—React Query records the mutation error, but this component receives only the pending state and silently restores the button without any explanation. Pass the mutation error into this surface and render its cause so an explicitly requested external operation cannot fail invisibly.

codex_findings.title: Honor the persisted Home tile visibility settings
codex_findings.detail: When a user has disabled `insight-loop`, `deadlines`, or `today` in `kitty-dashboard-config`, this unconditional surface still displays notices sourced from those features. The old returned-insight mount respected `visibleTiles['insight-loop']`, and the existing deadline and today panels remain gated, so the new projection bypasses the user's persisted visibility choices. Filter sources according to `visibleTiles` or introduce a separately configurable intelligence tile.

codex_findings.title: Preserve controls for responding to due insights
codex_findings.detail: When an insight becomes due, this replacement leaves `HomeIntelligence` as the mounted Home surface, but it only offers `onDiscuss`; the removed `InsightReturnCard` was the sole UI consumer of `useRespondToLoopInsight` and supplied act, snooze, and archive actions. Discussing a projected item does not change its pending status, so due insights can no longer be acknowledged or suppressed and continue returning indefinitely. Keep the existing response card mounted or wire equivalent lifecycle actions into this surface.

codex_findings.title: Clear context refs when closing the active chat
codex_findings.detail: When a user selects one or more context chips and then closes the active chat before sending, `handleCloseChat` switches `activeChatId` directly and never executes this reset in `handleSelectChat`. The chips therefore remain attached to the composer for the replacement chat, and the next send appends references selected for the closed conversation. Clear the refs in the active-close path or keep composer drafts scoped by chat ID.

codex_findings.title: Preserve explicit context during budget fitting
codex_findings.detail: In a standard-tier chat, one near-8,000-character text artifact already exceeds the 8,000-unit envelope once the normal bundle, runtime, safety context, and current message are included; multiple selected artifacts make this more likely. Appending the explicit block to `bundle_system` causes `_fit_final_model_messages` to prefix-clip it like optional enrichment, potentially truncating the selected document mid-content or dropping later references while only logging a server warning. Treat user-selected context as an atomic required block or reject/explicitly report references that cannot fit.

codex_findings.title: Surface a connection after an explicit refresh
codex_findings.detail: When three higher-ranked candidates already exist—for example, three `needs_jacob` deadlines—the explicit connection refresh generates and caches Magic results but immediately returns the same top-three projection, because every Magic score is at most 90 while deadlines score 100. The user clicks “find connections” and sees no visible result or acknowledgment even though generation succeeded. Ensure the refresh response includes at least one generated connection or return a separate refresh result that the UI can surface.

review_units.title: fix(builder): harden free packet execution
review_units.head: a19902be93a1439c44721e1d67d4bc59d02b2c8f

codex_findings.title: Keep reviewer evidence inputs read-only
codex_findings.detail: On the supported macOS Seatbelt path, this grants the model-controlled reviewer write access not only to its result but also to the staged bundle, implementation receipt, context manifest, and reviewer binding. The adapter validates their hashes before launching OpenCode but never revalidates them afterward, and its Git fingerprint records only the unchanged untracked filenames, so a reviewer using its allowed bash tool can rewrite acceptance criteria or evidence and then approve against those altered inputs without detection. Stage the inputs before entering the lower-trust boundary or expose only the result as writable and verify all input hashes after review.

codex_findings.title: Reject invalid startup timeouts before walking the ladder
codex_findings.detail: When `KB_MODEL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is non-numeric or non-positive, `run_with_timeout.py` exits before launching OpenCode, but this loop treats that configuration failure as a clean model failure, retries every model, and finally returns exit 75; Builder then durably records provider exhaustion even though no provider was contacted. Values such as `nan` are also accepted by the runner and silently disable the startup deadline. codex_findings.title: Keep Claude lifecycle handoffs routable
codex_findings.detail: Do not retire `claude` while the configured Claude lifecycle hooks still send as that participant. `.claude/hooks/session-end.sh:70` posts every automatic fallback with `--as claude`, and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh:82` uses the same sender when replaying the outbox; both calls are now rejected by `validate_active_participant()`, so fallbacks are queued indefinitely and no Claude session handoff reaches `workspace_global`.

codex_findings.title: Fail the turn when selected context cannot resolve
codex_findings.detail: When a selected project, artifact, or conversation is deleted, unreadable, or corrupt between selection and send, this catches the resolution failure and returns only a warning. `chat_completions()` merely appends those warnings to the internal bundle and continues normally, so the user receives an answer that silently omitted context they explicitly selected; propagate a contextual error or expose a visible partial-context warning instead.

codex_findings.title: Open the selected project workspace from Home
codex_findings.detail: The Home notice control is labelled “Open project,” but this handler only starts an active-project mutation and navigates to the generic Projects list. `ProjectsPanel` opens its workspace solely from its private `workspaceProjectId`, which this path never sets, so clicking a project-specific deadline or life notice does not open the owning workspace and may land on the list before project activation has even succeeded.

codex_findings.title: Show intelligence failures when no notices load
codex_findings.detail: Render an error/degraded state before returning for an empty item list. `HomeState` passes only `intelligence.data`, so an initial `/intelligence` request failure produces `projection === undefined`, while a successful response in which every collector is unavailable produces zero items; both cases hit this return and hide all evidence that personal-intelligence data could not be loaded.

codex_findings.title: Wait for active-project resolution before submitting
codex_findings.detail: When this view opens before `useActiveProject()` has resolved, `projectId` is temporarily `null` and the submit button remains enabled, so a user who submits during that window creates an unscoped run even though a persisted active project exists. The same fallback hides an active-project query failure and misleadingly says there is no active project; distinguish loading/error from a confirmed projectless state and prevent submission until the scope is known.

codex_findings.title: Show polling failures even when cached runs exist
codex_findings.detail: When the initial runs request succeeds but a later 3-second refetch fails, TanStack Query retains the previous `data` while setting `error`, so this condition suppresses the failure message. A running job can then remain visibly stuck at an old stage while the Gateway is unavailable, with no indication that the displayed state is stale; render a degraded/error notice alongside cached results whenever `runs.error` is set.

codex_findings.title: Surface report preview load failures
codex_findings.detail: When `GET /artifacts/{id}` fails or the artifact no longer exists, `useArtifact()` supplies an error with no data and this branch returns `null`. Clicking “Open report” therefore produces no dialog, alert, or recovery action, hiding the unavailable artifact evidence from the user; render the loading and error states instead of treating every missing `data` value as an invisible preview.

codex_findings.title: Route navigation to the Research workspace
codex_findings.detail: Remove this redirect now that `ResearchView` is implemented. Both the capability launcher (`page.tsx:253-256`) and Activity Center handler (`page.tsx:234-243`) reach destinations through `setActiveView()`, whose canonicalization applies this map, so every attempt to open `research` is converted to `library`; because Research is also absent from the rail, the new workspace and its Start research control are unreachable.

codex_findings.title: Reject unknown OpenViking modes
codex_findings.detail: If `KITTY_OPENVIKING_MODE` contains a typo or unsupported value, this silently converts it to `off`, so an operator who intended `shadow` or `context` gets no retrieval and no diagnostic that configuration is invalid. Validate the value and raise a contextual configuration error rather than inventing the disabled default.

codex_findings.title: Commit the artifact and run completion atomically
codex_findings.detail: If the process stops or `complete_run()` fails after this registration succeeds, the artifact row remains ready and discoverable while the research run has no `artifact_id` and is later marked failed or interrupted. This creates contradictory durable state and an orphaned report that cannot be opened from its run; register the artifact and transition the run in one database transaction, or add deterministic recovery for the partial state.

codex_findings.title: Log background research failures with their traceback
codex_findings.detail: When research, artifact registration, or persistence raises, this handler records a failed row and then returns normally without logging or re-raising the exception. Consequently FastAPI sees the background task as successful and operators lose the traceback and request context needed to diagnose the failure; record the durable failure but also emit the exception visibly, as other persisted background workers do.

codex_findings.title: Reject corrupt source data instead of replacing it
codex_findings.detail: If a persisted `sources_json` value is malformed, this decoder silently substitutes an empty list and returns the run as otherwise valid. That hides durable-state corruption and makes the UI report that recorded sources disappeared; raise a contextual `ResearchRunError` instead so the read path exposes the damaged run and database evidence.

codex_findings.title: Report unavailable research backends as failed runs
codex_findings.detail: When `TAVILY_API_KEY` is absent or Tavily returns a timeout/auth/server error, `_find_sources()` returns an empty list, and this new branch converts that failure into a normal report. `run_persisted_research()` then creates an artifact and marks the run `completed`, so the workspace presents an external-service outage as successful research with no sources. Preserve the distinction between a valid zero-result search and an unavailable backend, and let the latter mark the run failed with the real error context.

codex_findings.title: Propagate synthesis failures out of structured reports
codex_findings.detail: Separately from the Tavily search failure already reported, when the OpenRouter synthesis call times out, rejects authentication, or otherwise raises, `_synthesize_findings()` converts that exception into a failure sentence; this new return then packages the sentence as a valid report, allowing `run_persisted_research()` to save an artifact and mark the run completed. Propagate a typed synthesis error instead so the durable run records the provider failure rather than presenting unsynthesized evidence as successful research.

codex_findings.title: Validate project scope before creating the run
codex_findings.detail: When a client posts any positive but nonexistent `project_id`, this call accepts it and persists the run; artifact registration later also accepts the same value because neither table has a project foreign key. The completed report is therefore labelled as attached to a project that does not exist and cannot be reached through a real project workspace, so the project must be resolved before scheduling the run.

codex_findings.title: Update the stale agent destination assertion
codex_findings.detail: Change this expectation to `agent-sessions`: the changed projection now emits that destination at `gateway/activity_projection.py:144`, and a later regression test in this same file already expects it. The required CI pytest job runs all of `tests/`, so this assertion deterministically fails `test_activity_projection_normalizes_existing_authorities` and blocks the merge gate.

codex_findings.detail: Because this public repository's `pull_request_target` workflow runs `agent-review` for every non-draft `opened` and `synchronize` event, an external contributor can repeatedly push PR heads and cause paid OpenRouter requests using the repository secret.
