codex_findings.title: Route DeepSeek-authored PRs to another reviewer family
codex_findings.detail: When a PR was implemented by DeepSeek—for example, the configured frontier worker—the unconditional model here reviews it with DeepSeek as well. For sensitive scope, `scripts/pr_policy.py` accepts this workflow's exact-head `NO_ACTIONABLE_FINDINGS` comment as independent-review evidence, so a same-family review can satisfy the merge gate; select the PR reviewer from recorded worker provenance or use the configured non-DeepSeek reviewer for those heads.

codex_findings.title: Recalculate the documented routine spend for MiMo
codex_findings.detail: After declaring MiMo V2.5 as the routine implementation model here, the same document's routing and budget tables still price a routine pass as V4 Flash at CAD 0.0094 and derive the CAD 1.97 weekly estimate from that value. Using the checked-in token shape and price registry, the MiMo implementation pass costs CAD 0.05484 before adding its DeepSeek review, versus CAD 0.00938 for Flash, so operators relying on this guidance underestimate routine implementation spend by roughly 5.8×; update the route, per-pass cost, and weekly projection for the configured MiMo/DeepSeek pair.

review_units.title: feat(builder): harden unattended autonomy
review_units.head: b6d014986a4fc01bbf91cecd5e2ad7aeee28845e

codex_findings.title: Reserve for every paid reviewer attempted
codex_findings.detail: When MiniMax consumes billable tokens but exits without writing a review, the adapter proceeds to this Qwen fallback, while `resolve_paid_route()` reserves and later records only the maximum cost of one reviewer candidate rather than the sum of sequential attempts. The cheap lane can therefore be admitted with roughly CAD 0.0439 remaining yet spend up to roughly CAD 0.0624 for the worker plus both reviewers, overrunning and understating the governed weekly reserve; include the fallback attempt in the worst-case projection or only hand off when the primary provably incurred no usage.

codex_findings.title: Report malformed packet registries instead of dropping them
codex_findings.detail: When any `*.source.json` slate is unreadable or contains malformed JSON, this silently omits the entire slate and `status()` still emits an apparently valid runway from incomplete coverage. That can incorrectly report `caught_up`, low-water, or refill decisions precisely when the source evidence is unavailable; propagate a contextual error or surface the registry failure in reconciliation instead.

codex_findings.title: Reject null packet arrays instead of treating them as empty
codex_findings.detail: When a source slate contains a missing, null, or otherwise falsy `packets` value, `slate.get("packets") or []` normalizes the malformed field to an empty list before the type check, silently dropping the slate and allowing `status()` to report incomplete runway or even `caught_up`. Fresh evidence after the JSON/read fix is that structurally invalid packet arrays still bypass `PacketRegistryError`; validate the raw field before applying any empty-list default.

codex_findings.title: Stop deriving unresolved state from retained packet prose
codex_findings.detail: Once an interactive packet is completed but its versioned Markdown contract remains in `docs/packets/`, every supervisor status call still synthesizes `status: unresolved` solely from the document headers. `_classify_registry()` then keeps counting that historical packet as actionable, preventing truthful `caught_up` and distorting low-water/refill decisions; obtain lifecycle state from a supported registry/projection rather than inferring it from document existence.

codex_findings.title: Treat the repository root as a forbidden-path wildcard
codex_findings.detail: For a valid packet with `forbidden_paths: ["."]`, `_parts(".")` is empty and this branch returns `False` against every changed path, so the deterministic gate records `passed: true` despite repository changes. The runner already defines `"."` as the whole-repository path grant; apply the same root-wildcard semantics here or reject this contract value during manifest validation.

codex_findings.title: Check both sides of renames in the contract gate
codex_findings.detail: When a worker renames a file from a forbidden directory into an allowed directory, Git's default rename detection makes this `--name-only` query return only the destination. The subsequent overlap check therefore sees no forbidden path and records `passed: true`; request rename status or use `--no-renames` so both the deleted source and added destination are evaluated.

codex_findings.title: Fail the contract gate when a changed file cannot be read
codex_findings.detail: If a changed regular file raises `OSError` while being inspected, this silently excludes it from the searched text. A packet containing only `forbidden_symbols` can therefore receive `passed: true` and proceed to validation/review even though the gate never inspected all changed files; raise `ContractGateError` with the affected path instead of treating unavailable evidence as absence.

codex_findings.title: Do not reset paid reviewer outage streaks
codex_findings.detail: When a paid DSH reviewer ladder exits 75, `review_provider_exhaustion` records the reason as `all configured free reviewer providers were unavailable`; this new condition then interprets every subsequent paid run as a free-to-paid lane change, appends a streak-breaking event, and resets the crash count. A persistent paid-reviewer outage therefore never reaches the recovery cap and can repeatedly spend on worker/reviewer attempts; classify the reviewer failure by its actual lane or restrict this reset to a genuinely prior free execution.

codex_findings.title: Recheck contract constraints after janitor mutations
codex_findings.detail: With `publication_preflight=True`, this gate runs before `apply_safe_repairs()`, which can subsequently modify and commit packet files through Ruff. For example, Ruff can remove an unused import named in `required_symbols`, or modify a forbidden subpath beneath a broad allowed path, yet the recorded gate remains `passed: true` and is never recomputed before validation/review; run the deterministic checks again after the janitor's final commit.

codex_findings.title: Let fenced recovery candidates pass the new preflight
codex_findings.detail: When `_dispatch_candidate()` returns a supported recovery candidate—a blocked task with a stale attempt—`preflight_packet()` derives `not_queued` for every blocked task and returns `PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED`, so this condition skips it on every real `tick()` even though `run_packet()` is designed to reconcile exactly that state. This disables unattended crash recovery; preserve the durable recovery classification when applying preflight.

codex_findings.title: Apply the new admission gates to dispatchable counts
codex_findings.detail: When an otherwise queued packet has a stale allowed path, an existing Builder PR, or unavailable GitHub/main truth, this new branch makes `tick()` skip it, but `dispatchable_counts()` still uses only `_dispatch_candidate()` and therefore counts it as launchable. `control_plane_summary()` consequently reports `eligible_now > 0` to the Work UI even though every supervisor tick will refuse the work; derive the count through the same reconciliation and preflight path or expose it as a weaker pre-admission count.

codex_findings.title: Keep unattended dispatches on the authorized free lane
codex_findings.detail: Whenever the periodic supervisor selects an eligible packet, this unconditionally invokes `--paid --tier cheap`, so an unattended tick can spend money without a packet-specific or operator paid-route decision. The bundled autonomy design explicitly retains free execution and forbids new paid routing; preserve `--free` here unless an explicit, durable authorization selects a paid route.

codex_findings.title: Preflight the route the supervisor actually launches
codex_findings.detail: Even with the paid route authorized, packets using the canonical omitted `policy.routing` are preflighted as free at CAD 0, while this command always launches `--paid --tier cheap`. When the remaining reserve is below the configured cheap-route cost, each tick admits and spawns the packet, then `_governor_gate()` rejects the child before it can durably claim the task, causing the same failed dispatch every interval; run admission against the actual cheap route and its configured cost.

codex_findings.title: Treat the root allowlist as overlapping every change
codex_findings.detail: For `allowed_paths=["."]`, which the existing runner contract explicitly treats as access to the entire repository (`tests/test_builder_runner.py:579-580`), filtering out `"."` leaves an empty tuple and this helper returns `False` against every changed path. The stale-base gate therefore admits a broad packet after arbitrary changes on main; represent the repository root as a wildcard instead of no path.

codex_findings.title: Include both sides of renames in freshness checks
codex_findings.detail: When main renames a file from an allowed path to a destination outside that path, `git diff --name-only` reports only the rename destination, so the old allowed path is absent and `relevant_paths_changed` remains empty. The packet is then dispatched against a base whose target file was removed; use Git's documented rename status or disable rename detection so both source and destination are checked ([git-diff options](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff)).

codex_findings.title: Bind PR collisions to the Builder repository
codex_findings.detail: When a fork opens a PR whose source branch has the same `kittybuilder/<task-id>` name as a queued Builder task, this snapshot keys both PRs solely by `headRefName`, so `_select_packets()` treats the fork PR as Builder publication evidence and skips the legitimate task. `gh pr list --help` explicitly notes that owner-qualified head filtering is unsupported and exposes `headRepositoryOwner` and `isCrossRepository` as separate JSON fields; request and verify those fields, or bind the PR by repository owner plus expected head OID, before allowing it to override durable Builder work.

codex_findings.title: Remove ambient tokens from GitHub reconciliation
codex_findings.detail: When the launchd wrapper loads `.env`, or an interactive caller exports `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, this `gh pr list` subprocess inherits those credentials. `gh help environment` states that these variables take precedence over stored credentials, so a stale or insufficiently scoped ambient token makes the snapshot unavailable and blocks every supervisor tick even when valid keyring auth exists; pass a sanitized environment that removes both variables, as the existing publish runner does.

codex_findings.title: Reject non-array GitHub snapshots
codex_findings.detail: When `gh pr list` returns valid JSON with the wrong top-level shape, such as `{}`, decoding succeeds and the subsequent loop silently produces an empty `by_head` map marked `available: true`. A tick can then launch a packet despite an existing open or merged Builder PR because malformed external evidence was treated as authoritative absence; require `rows` to be a list of objects and return an unavailable snapshot with the offending shape otherwise.

codex_findings.title: Keep free review disjoint from implementation
codex_findings.detail: The free reviewer always uses `openrouter/free`, which is also the worker ladder's final entry and may select the same Poolside or Tencent backing model used for implementation. Because `chosen_model` is never propagated into reviewer candidate selection, a free implementation can be approved by the same model family; bind the reviewer route to the recorded worker model and exclude that family.

codex_findings.title: Allow the reviewer to create its staged prompt
codex_findings.detail: On the supported macOS runtime, `_run_review_command()` executes this script with `worktree_writable=False` and allowlists only the five `.kittybuilder-review-*.json` staging files. This redirect creates a new `.kittybuilder-review-prompt-*.txt` path that is absent from that allowlist, so Seatbelt denies the write and every Builder review exits before DSH launches; add this exact path to the reviewer boundary or create the prompt under the writable runtime directory.

codex_findings.title: Authenticate the free OpenRouter lane
codex_findings.detail: When `--free` is selected, every configured worker model here—and the free reviewer default—uses OpenRouter, but `build_child_environment()` creates a fresh empty `HOME` and strips ambient credentials while `_sanitize_free_adapter_env()` supplies no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`; only the paid route restores that key. Explicit free runs therefore reach DSH without an environment key or credential store and exhaust before any model can run; provide a scoped authentication boundary for free OpenRouter requests without enabling paid fallback.

codex_findings.title: Preserve usable time for fallback models
codex_findings.detail: If the first DSH provider hangs or never starts, this invocation gives it almost the entire 3,600-second worker budget and no longer passes the removed OpenCode adapter's JSON-event/startup-timeout controls. After that timeout, `model_timeout()` gives each remaining fallback only one second, so the ladder cannot recover from the startup hangs it is intended to survive; enforce a bounded startup window or reserve meaningful time for later candidates.

codex_findings.title: Pass the provider credential through the isolation boundary
codex_findings.detail: For a launchd-started paid run, sourcing `.env` here does not actually authenticate the OpenRouter worker: `run_worker()` later constructs its model environment with `build_child_environment()`, which retains only locale variables and assigns a fresh empty `HOME`, while the paid adapter environment contains model names but no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Consequently the newly hard-coded paid supervisor route exhausts every provider instead of executing; supply the credential through a narrowly supported child boundary or retain the free route.

review_units.title: feat(image): expose resolved model in estimate
review_units.head: fc77d165fad62910202ee01bf35bcc5e98eaaa8f

codex_findings.title: Keep runtime-selected Draw Things model unresolved
codex_findings.detail: When `auto_route` selects the Draw Things recipe, this now calls `_iteration_model_id`, which returns `drawthings@<dt_url>` from `mcp/imagen/engines/drawthings.py:39-40`; that value identifies the endpoint, while the actual model is selected separately through `settings.dt_model` at dispatch (`drawthings.py:64-65`). The estimate therefore exposes and groups observations under a made-up exact model identifier instead of preserving `null` for this runtime-selected provider; exclude Draw Things from this recipe-aware resolution path until its actual installed model can be determined.

review_units.title: kittybuilder: [KF-UNDO-02] Todo-create undo is durable and partial failure is truthful
review_units.head: f34673e143ac42e5da6984be8146b6fa3c8aabf7

codex_findings.title: Guard compensation against newer todo changes
codex_findings.detail: If journal recording fails while another gateway process completes or otherwise changes this newly created todo, this unconditional delete succeeds and removes that newer mutation; `execute()` then records the action as safely compensated and failed. The direct todo routes mutate through the same storage seam without journal fencing, so compensation should delete only when the row still matches the created snapshot, otherwise preserve it and report an unknown outcome.

codex_findings.title: Preserve failure context in unknown action receipts
codex_findings.detail: When journal recording fails and the compensating deletion also raises, this branch converts both exceptions into a generic `UNKNOWN_OUTCOME` result. The durable action returned by `/actions` therefore omits the actual journal and compensation causes needed for the requested manual review, leaving that evidence only in potentially transient logs. Persist the exception types/messages and relevant operation context in the action result or another durable record.

codex_findings.title: Treat an already-absent todo as compensated
codex_findings.detail: When journal recording fails and another request has already removed the newly created todo before compensation runs, `delete_todo()` returns `False` because its `DELETE ... WHERE id = ?` matched no row. That still proves the created entity is absent, but this branch records a terminal `unknown` outcome and requests unnecessary manual review. Treat the absent row as a successful compensation, while retaining the original journal failure as the action's failure cause.

codex_findings.title: Commit the undo receipt atomically with execution
codex_findings.detail: If the gateway exits after `undo_journal.record()` commits but before this `_finish()` commits, the todo and journal entry survive while the action remains `executing`; startup reconciliation then marks the action `unknown` and explicitly stores `undo_journal_id = NULL`. The action API consequently loses the promised durable receipt even though a valid undo entry exists. Persist the journal entry and action receipt in one transaction, or make reconciliation recover the receipt instead of severing the link.

codex_findings.title: Make the schema addition recoverable after partial application
codex_findings.detail: If the process exits after this `ALTER TABLE` succeeds but before `_apply_migration()` records the migration name—or if the following index statement fails—the column remains committed while `053_action_undo_receipt.sql` remains pending. Every later startup then retries this statement and fails with `duplicate column name: undo_journal_id`, preventing migration and gateway initialization; wrap the migration and its marker in one transaction or otherwise make the column addition safely replayable.

codex_findings.title: Refuse undo after the todo has changed
codex_findings.detail: If a user completes a todo through `/todos/{todo_id}/complete` after this create receipt is issued and then invokes the receipt, this branch deletes the completed todo without noticing the newer mutation. Todo completion and the other direct todo routes do not append journal entries, so the journal's newer-entry conflict guard cannot protect this path; compare the current todo with the recorded `after` snapshot (or journal all todo mutations) before deleting it.

codex_findings.title: Commit todo deletion and undo completion together
codex_findings.detail: When the gateway exits or the journal write fails after this call returns, `delete_todo()` has already committed the deletion but `undo()` has not yet marked the receipt undone or inserted its restoration entry. The durable receipt therefore remains pending even though its effect happened, and retrying it only reports that the todo is missing; make the deletion and journal transition atomic or add recovery that can durably recognize this completed undo.

review_units.title: feat(agent-room): expose global room in Agents view
review_units.head: f9e6c6aa7ef3f29b7330f133319d9b7e523f2846

codex_findings.title: Preserve action failures across successful polls
codex_findings.detail: A successful three-second refresh unconditionally clears the shared error state, including an unresolved send or acknowledgement failure. If a post is rejected shortly before the next poll, its alert can disappear almost immediately while the draft remains unsent, hiding the failure from the user; keep polling errors separate from mutation errors or clear an action error only after that action is retried successfully.

codex_findings.title: Render inbox messages outside the transcript window
codex_findings.detail: Because these requests independently fetch the newest 100 room messages and the newest 100 messages addressed to Jacob, the inbox can contain an unread message that is absent from `recent`—for example, after more than 100 newer agent-to-agent messages. That message increases the unread count but is never rendered, so Jacob has no way to inspect or acknowledge the item that the UI says needs attention; merge inbox-only messages into the display or provide a dedicated inbox view.

codex_findings.title: Prevent stale polls from overwriting newer mutations
codex_findings.detail: When a scheduled poll overlaps a send or acknowledgement, its snapshot can have been read before the mutation but resolve afterward. These unconditional replacements then make a successfully posted message disappear or revert an acknowledged receipt until the next poll; sequence snapshots against mutations, merge them monotonically, or force a refresh after the in-flight poll finishes.

codex_findings.title: Allow seen messages to be acknowledged
codex_findings.detail: When a durable receipt is already `seen` but not `acknowledged`—for example, because Jacob viewed it through another client—`unreadIds.has(message.id)` is false, so this condition removes the only acknowledgement control. Since the inbox deliberately includes all receipt states, the button should remain available whenever `acknowledged_at` is null, regardless of whether `seen_at` is already set.

codex_findings.title: Hide room-state claims until the room loads
codex_findings.detail: If the initial `Promise.all` fails because the Gateway is unavailable or misconfigured, `room` remains null but the screen still declares a durable room and four registered agents, renders an empty transcript, and enables the composer. This fabricates successful backend state precisely when evidence is unavailable; gate these claims and controls on a loaded room and expose a clear retry/degraded state instead.

codex_findings.title: Load reply context beyond the recent-message window
codex_findings.detail: When a recent reply points to a parent older than the 100-message transcript window, this lookup returns no parent and the reply trail is silently omitted even though `parent_message_id` is present. The UI then displays a threaded response without indicating what it answers; fetch the thread/parent when it is missing from the local map or include enough parent context in the response.

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed message payloads
codex_findings.detail: When the Gateway returns a successful but malformed response such as `{}` or `{ messages: null }`, this fallback converts unavailable evidence into an authoritative empty transcript. During polling, `setMessages(recent)` then erases the last durable transcript and clears the error instead of preserving the prior state. Validate that `messages` is an array and throw a descriptive payload error; the inbox helper has the same issue.

codex_findings.title: Remove the unrenderable Research view
codex_findings.detail: Registering `research` makes `canonicalActiveView` accept it, but the reviewed tree contains no `ResearchView` and no `case 'research'` in `ViewRenderer`, so a persisted or programmatically selected Research view falls through to `null` and produces a blank application surface. Add the corresponding renderer before treating this ID as valid, or leave it out of the registry.

review_units.title: docs(agent-room): make global room default continuity
review_units.head: aadc0a06f9c7c908002c8071804640f036b34b54

codex_findings.title: Keep fallback checkpoints out of the normal receipt
codex_findings.detail: When `workspace_global` is available but either legacy checkpoint is malformed, divergent, or contains an invalid PR claim, step 1 has already run the full `./kitty context --agent`: `gateway.context_receipt.inspect_continuity()` unconditionally loads and validates both files, failures make the receipt exit nonzero, and `build_context_receipt()` still exports STATE's `blockers` and `next_action`. A bare continuation can therefore stop or inherit legacy state before reaching the room-based resolution described here; use a receipt mode that excludes legacy continuity when the room is available, or make those checks non-blocking in that mode.

codex_findings.title: Validate the legacy fallback when the room has no handoff
codex_findings.detail: When the room is reachable but the unread inbox is empty and no thread ID is known, these lines select the legacy checkpoint fallback, yet the command sequence above has explicitly skipped all legacy checks and `session_end_survey.sh` only parses carried recommendations rather than validating checkpoint identity. The strict receipt is reserved for total room unavailability, so this common fallback can trust a stale, divergent, or malformed checkpoint; run legacy validation whenever this branch is selected, not only when the room call itself fails.

codex_findings.title: Validate the final state before posting the handoff
codex_findings.detail: Whenever session-end writes the compatibility snapshots, this publishes the primary handoff before those tracked-file mutations and before step 12 runs `check_continuity_state.py`, the context receipt, and the final Git inspection. If a write or validation fails—or merely changes the dirty-path inventory—the durable room message already advertises pre-final SHA/evidence and no later step updates it; post after final validation or require a correcting reply containing the verified final state.

codex_findings.title: Retrieve assignment-scoped room messages
codex_findings.detail: Once the room has more than 100 messages, these fallback commands cannot reliably implement “relevant”: checking `./kitty room recent --help` and `inbox --help` shows only bounded list controls, while `gateway/agent_room_cli.py` defaults both commands to 100 entries, invokes inbox without `--unread`, and provides no assignment filter or cursor. An active handoff older than the newest window is therefore undiscoverable, while acknowledged broadcasts are repeatedly reloaded on normal starts; persist and retrieve the relevant thread ID, or add assignment/cursor filtering and use the unread inbox for discovery.

codex_findings.title: Use the GAR-safe receipt in the Claude bootloader
codex_findings.detail: When `workspace_global` is available, Claude still runs the strict legacy-compatible receipt here, which unconditionally validates `.claude/STATE.md` and `.claude/HANDOFF.md`; a stale or malformed compatibility file can therefore stop cold start before Claude follows the new room continuity, contrary to the adjacent statement that those files are only a fallback. codex_findings.title: Implement the documented legacy-skip receipt flag
codex_findings.detail: This command fails immediately in every GAR-available startup because the reviewed `gateway/context_receipt.py:1606-1628` registers only `--agent`, `--compact`, and `--skip-builder`; its help output contains no `--skip-legacy-continuity`, and the new focused tests fail with `unrecognized arguments`/unexpected-keyword errors. codex_findings.title: Make the contract assertion match the wrapped document text

review_units.head: 40ad64a2cf998338e51315242535df418c8c126e

codex_findings.title: Prevent broadcasts from starving unread direct messages
codex_findings.detail: `room inbox` is backed by `gateway.agent_workspace.list_inbox`, which returns both broadcasts and direct messages ordered newest-first. With this limit, 12 newer unread broadcasts exclude an older direct request to Claude; because the hook explicitly avoids acknowledging messages and tells Claude to ACK only directs, those broadcasts can occupy every subsequent SessionStart window indefinitely, so the direct request is never injected. Fetch direct messages separately or ensure the bounded window cannot starve them.

codex_findings.title: Preserve GAR command errors at session start
codex_findings.detail: When either room command fails because of a database, schema, permission, or CLI error, these calls discard all stderr and collapse both statuses into `GAR_OK=0`; the hook then prints the same generic “unavailable” warning and exits successfully. That makes the actual continuity failure impossible to diagnose or repair from the hook output. Capture and report each failed command's status, parameters, and response context, retrying first if appropriate.

codex_findings.title: Cap GAR injection by total content size
codex_findings.detail: When the latest 12 messages are max-sized unread messages addressed to Claude, both commands emit the same full 12,000-character contents, so this hook injects roughly 288,000 characters plus metadata on every start or resume. Limiting row count alone therefore still allows tens of thousands of tokens of duplicated lifecycle context to crowd out the actual conversation. Truncate individual messages, enforce a total output budget, and deduplicate inbox entries already present in the recent window.

codex_findings.title: Do not run session-end on every assistant turn
codex_findings.detail: Claude Code invokes the Stop hook whenever the main agent finishes a response, not only when the user is closing the session, so this unconditional block forces `/session-end` after an ordinary answer or intermediate work update. That skill performs the full survey, continuity/KB writes, and then stops rather than continuing the assignment; after a receipt is accepted the start marker is also removed, so the next turn cannot recognize any receipt and is forced through the workflow again. Gate this on an explicit session-ending signal instead of every Stop event.

codex_findings.title: Keep the stop blocked when the durable handoff fails
codex_findings.detail: On the continuation Stop pass, if `kitty room recent` is unavailable, `room post` fails, or the final assistant message is empty, this path only warns and then exits successfully. No GAR receipt is created and the scratchpad fallback merely prints another warning, so the session can end with the continuity data this feature promises to preserve permanently lost. Retry or return another blocking decision with the actual command failure instead of failing open.

codex_findings.title: Add the implementations required by these regression tests
codex_findings.detail: On exact commit `891100e`, running `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_agent_room_global.py tests/test_agent_room_lifecycle_hooks.py tests/test_agent_room_lifecycle_review_regressions.py` produces 9 failures and 8 passes: `.claude/settings.json` has neither the asserted Stop prompt nor a SessionEnd hook, `.claude/hooks/session-end.sh` is absent, and the room API/CLI and start hook do not implement `direct_only`, `--direct-only`, or durable-outbox flushing. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier runtime comments is that this target newly adds regression tests for those remedies without adding the corresponding production changes, so the focused suite is unconditionally red; land the implementations with the tests.

review_units.head: b28ea08e33e40bc8f2b9c0f02694a6eb8b0e44ce

codex_findings.title: Exclude paused initiatives from usable runway
codex_findings.detail: When an operator-paused initiative has queued packets waiting on dependencies, `_classify_builder_status` places them in `pending_backend` before its paused-state check, and this new sum therefore treats work that Builder cannot dispatch as usable runway. Six such packets make replenishment report `runway_healthy` even when there is no active unattended work, so the slate author never restores the runway until the paused initiative is resumed or removed.

codex_findings.title: Fail closed on unreadable replenisher receipts
codex_findings.detail: If `replenisher-status.json` is temporarily unreadable or malformed while its recorded author process is still running, this converts the evidence failure into “no receipt”; the low-water path can then launch a second slate author and overwrite the original receipt, defeating the single-flight guarantee and potentially duplicating costly external work. Distinguish a missing file from read/parse failure and refuse to launch when existing receipt evidence cannot be trusted.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the slate-author configuration error
codex_findings.detail: When `KITTY_BUILDER_SLATE_AUTHOR_ARGV_JSON` is malformed, names a missing/non-executable file, or points outside the trusted repo, this catch discards the specific `SupervisorError` and exposes only `invalid_author_config`. Operators cannot tell which configuration invariant failed or repair it from the tick/status receipt, contrary to the repository's fail-loud requirement; return the safe exception detail alongside the reason rather than swallowing it.

codex_findings.title: Load only the provider key into the DSH process
codex_findings.detail: When the repository `.env` contains other credentials such as `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `load_env_assignments` exports every dotenv assignment before executing DSH, so both the model-controlled worker and reviewer inherit all of those secrets rather than only the required `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. This bypasses the runner's secret-free child environment and credential blocklist; filter the loaded assignments to the provider credential instead of sourcing the complete repository environment.

codex_findings.title: Avoid signaling process group zero in cleanup
codex_findings.detail: If replenishment returns `launched: false` without a PID—for example because `Popen` fails—the preceding assertion raises and this `finally` block evaluates the fallback as PID 0. On POSIX, `kill(0, 9)` sends SIGKILL to the entire current process group, so a normal test failure can terminate pytest and its CI shell instead of reporting the actual launch error; only call `os.kill` after validating a strictly positive returned PID.

codex_findings.title: Keep unparsed calendar timestamps from appearing twice
codex_findings.detail: On Macs using a 24-hour clock or a non-English locale, the English AM/PM regex does not match, so this fallback assigns the identical raw timestamp to both `start_date` and `start_time`. The upcoming-calendar renderer treats both as parsed and concatenates them at `DashboardView.tsx:266`, displaying values such as `Thursday, ... 14:30 Thursday, ... 14:30`; leave one fallback field empty or explicitly distinguish successful parsing.

codex_findings.title: Raise the day-palette text contrast
codex_findings.detail: In the day/cosmic dashboard, `inkFaint` has only about 3.30:1 contrast on `cream` and 3.02:1 on `creamSoft`, while `orange` on `cream` is about 3.56:1. These colors are used for 10.5–12.5px labels, inactive tabs, timestamps, and action text, all below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA requirement for normal text; darken the day-palette values or reserve these colors for non-text decoration.

codex_findings.title: Do not invent clear weather when conditions are missing
codex_findings.detail: When wttr.in returns a usable temperature but omits or empties `weatherDesc`, `gateway/weather.py:52-54` produces a weather object with an empty description, so this new fallback reports the conditions as `clear` without evidence. Display an unavailable/unknown condition or omit the description instead of turning a partial upstream response into a potentially false weather claim.

codex_findings.title: Do not report failed calendar reads as an empty schedule
codex_findings.detail: When Calendar exists but access is denied or AppleScript returns another nonzero status, `is_available()` still returns true because it ignores `returncode` (`gateway/calendar_integration.py:169-174`), while `get_today()` converts the failed read to `[]` (`gateway/calendar_integration.py:99-101`) and the route labels that result available. Consequently this new branch tells the user there is nothing scheduled even though the calendar was never read, which could cause appointments to be missed; preserve the read failure through the route and render an unavailable/error state instead.

codex_findings.title: Preserve all-day calendar semantics
codex_findings.detail: For all-day Calendar events, the AppleScript bridge emits only summary, start date, and end date (`gateway/calendar_integration.py:88-92`) and drops Calendar's all-day property, so this new schedule always renders the midnight-derived `start_time` as if it were a timed appointment. Carry an `all_day` field through the response and display `all day`; otherwise birthdays, holidays, and other all-day entries misleadingly appear scheduled at 12:00 AM.

codex_findings.title: Preserve project-query failures in the dashboard
codex_findings.detail: When `/projects` fails, `KittyContext` exposes `projectsQuery.data ?? []`, and this dashboard consumes only that empty array, causing `ProjectsTile` to display `0` and `none yet` instead of indicating that project data is unavailable. Pass the query loading/error state into the dashboard or read `k.projectsQuery` here so a gateway failure cannot be mistaken for a genuinely empty project list.

codex_findings.title: Allow for the calendar availability probe in the timeout
codex_findings.detail: When the availability probe takes more than one second and the subsequent Calendar read approaches its 15-second backend timeout, this 16-second client deadline aborts a request that the server still considers in progress. `gateway/routes/calendar.py:16-18` first runs `is_available()` with its own five-second timeout and only then starts the 15-second read, so the endpoint can legitimately take almost 20 seconds; account for both operations or remove the duplicate probe before claiming this stays above the backend deadline.

review_units.head: 9ff0065ef4d362cc2e6d9a5d9e854795ac52f4e3

codex_findings.title: Fail when the canonical Builder root cannot be resolved
codex_findings.detail: When Git is unavailable, incompatible, or the linked-worktree metadata cannot be resolved, this command suppresses the error and returns success; `canonical_root` then remains the current worktree, so the Gateway can silently open a per-worktree Builder database while the canonical CLI uses another database. Raise the resolution error with its status and context instead of silently restoring the split-state behavior.

codex_findings.title: Apply canonical Builder state to the production launcher
codex_findings.detail: When production mode is intentionally installed from a linked worktree using the supported `scripts/kitty_desktop_launchd.py install --allow-worktree-install` path, launchd executes `gateway/start_gateway.sh` directly and its plist provides neither `KITTY_BUILDER_DATA_DIR` nor `KITTY_DATA_ROOT`. Because canonicalization is invoked only by `cmd_up` and `cmd_run_fg`, that Gateway still defaults to the linked worktree's `data/kittybuilder` while `./kitty builder` uses the Git common root; move the derivation into the shared Gateway bootstrap or include it in the generated launchd environment.

review_units.title: fix(builder): restore reliable no-spend Work proposal routing
review_units.head: 338527d13f2aea2a728a0f92638062cd4f725e0f

codex_findings.title: Project persisted approval fields into Work
codex_findings.detail: This branch can never succeed for a real `/work` response: `gateway.builder_status._read_initiatives` does not select the newly added approval columns, and `_initiative_projection` never constructs an `approval` object. Reproducing the production projection after applying an approval-bound manifest yields `evidence.approval.state == "unavailable"`, so Work falsely reports that every approved initiative lacks durable approval evidence. Feed the persisted binding through the supported Builder status projection rather than testing only a hand-built snapshot.

codex_findings.title: Preserve unexpected compiler failure evidence
codex_findings.detail: When `call_llm` or proposal processing raises an unexpected exception, this catch converts it into an untyped generic receipt before the route can log the exception. The HTTP wrapper therefore sees an ordinary return and responds 200 without an `error_code`, status, parameters, or response context, making provider and parsing regressions indistinguishable and leaving no actionable server-side failure at this layer. Log and raise a typed error with the original cause while separately translating safe user-facing copy.

codex_findings.title: Retry schema-invalid proposal objects
codex_findings.detail: The retry loop stops as soon as the model output parses to any JSON object, before checking required fields or normalizing its scope. Responses such as `{}`, an empty objective, a missing `allowed_paths`, or an unsafe path therefore bypass the second no-spend attempt and immediately return `proposal_invalid` or `proposal_scope_invalid`, even though they are unusable compiler outputs just like malformed JSON. Perform the required-field and scope validation inside the retry loop so the bounded retry covers structurally invalid model responses.

codex_findings.title: Reject model-generated shell validation commands
codex_findings.detail: The compiler accepts any string list returned in `validation_commands` and passes it into the approved manifest, while the proposal card never displays those commands. For a prompt-injected or simply erroneous model response, Builder later executes the hidden value with `shell=True` in `gateway.builder_attempt.run_validation`, so commands such as deletion or credential exfiltration can run after a generic approval click without the required explicit authorization. Validate against a strict command allowlist or require the exact commands to be visibly reviewed under the appropriate authorization tier.

codex_findings.title: Supply execution evidence before rendering it
codex_findings.detail: The new execution receipt UI is unreachable with production data because `_project_work_item` emits only validation, review, publication, and approval under `evidence`; it never emits `execution`, and the Builder status projection likewise does not attach the governor receipt. Consequently configured/actual provider, model, retries, and spend are shown only in tests that inject a synthetic field, while real Work rows never display them. Add this data to the supported projection or remove the dead presentation contract.

codex_findings.title: Keep browser storage optional for Builder proposals
codex_findings.detail: In browsers where `localStorage.getItem` throws—for example blocked storage, privacy restrictions, or a sandboxed embedding—this effect crashes the proposal card. The new Work host explicitly catches the same storage failure while recovering its optional ambiguity checkpoint, but mounting this child immediately performs the unguarded access again, so users cannot review or approve the freshly compiled proposal even though durable Builder state does not depend on browser storage. Catch the storage exception and continue without recovery, or show an actionable storage-specific error.

codex_findings.title: Allow enough time for both compile attempts
codex_findings.detail: The browser aborts this request after 65 seconds, but the default backend path performs two sequential provider calls with a 60-second timeout each. When the first attempt consumes its timeout—the transient no-response case the new retry is intended to recover—the client disconnects about five seconds into attempt two and reports failure even if that retry later succeeds. The request timeout needs to cover both attempts and overhead, or the backend needs a single overall deadline shorter than the client timeout.

codex_findings.title: Append `/api` for root Ollama URLs
codex_findings.detail: For the conventional Ollama base `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, the port heuristic selects `local_ollama` but constructs `http://127.0.0.1:11434/chat`; Ollama's native endpoint is `/api/chat`. The repository's other Ollama clients likewise accept the root base and append `/api/generate`, while the added test avoids the bug by supplying a pre-suffixed `/api` base. Normalize both root and `/api` forms before appending the chat path so the standard configuration does not receive a 404.

codex_findings.title: Keep saved-provider retry pinned to the selected route
codex_findings.detail: When the user clicks “Try saved provider route,” a failure or absence of the selected provider does not stay pinned: `allow_provider_fallback=True` continues into LiteLLM and then every configured provider in `effective_provider_order()`. This can send the request—and incur charges—through providers the user did not select, even though the UI and compiler metadata describe the action as the saved-provider route. Either call only the selected provider or relabel and separately authorize the exact automatic fallback/spend behavior.

review_units.title: feat(mission): native Mission integration — plan-review-gated Builder handoff
review_units.head: 2479d537570f13c9be58f5aa4b6fca2352325737

codex_findings.title: Observe startup review-recovery failures
codex_findings.detail: The startup recovery coroutine is detached with `create_task`, and shutdown awaits it only while it is still pending. If database initialization, Mission decoding, or reconciliation raises before shutdown, the completed task's exception is never retrieved, startup still succeeds, and pending reviews remain stranded with only an event-loop warning. Attach it to the supervised recovery machinery or always inspect/await its result so startup recovery fails visibly with its real cause.

codex_findings.title: Keep pending plans reviewable after HEAD advances
codex_findings.detail: A prepared plan commit branches from the checkout HEAD at proposal time. If that plan remains pending while the canonical checkout advances on another branch/commit, the old plan commit and the new source HEAD are siblings, so `merge-base --is-ancestor <new HEAD> <plan commit>` fails even though the stored plan commit is still valid and reachable. Startup recovery and later retries then permanently report the reviewer unavailable until the proposal is rebuilt; validate the plan against its recorded base instead of requiring it to descend from the current HEAD.

codex_findings.title: Compare the reviewer with the actual planner family
codex_findings.detail: This independence check only rejects Claude/Anthropic names, rather than comparing the reviewer with the model that produced the proposal or owns the implementation. In a non-Claude flow—such as a proposal compiled by Gemini, or an environment configured with a non-Claude Builder worker—the same model family can perform both sides of the required independent review while this function reports it as independent. Persist the planner/implementer identity and select a genuinely different reviewer family.

codex_findings.title: Preserve reviewer failure diagnostics
codex_findings.detail: When the DSH/OpenRouter subprocess exits nonzero, this replaces its exit status, provider/model parameters, stderr, and stdout with the generic message `independent reviewer is unavailable`. The resulting Automation run cannot distinguish authentication, quota, model, launcher, or malformed-request failures, leaving the required review gate stuck without an actionable cause; propagate bounded response context as the other Git subprocess helpers do.

codex_findings.title: Record the actual reviewed commit in review_head
codex_findings.detail: Whenever `review_checkout_sha` is supplied—which is the normal Mission plan path—the reviewer is detached at that plan commit, but the receipt records `source_before[0]`, the source checkout's base HEAD. Consequently `plan.review_evidence.review_head` identifies a commit the reviewer did not inspect and cannot serve as exact provenance; return the resolved checkout target instead.

codex_findings.title: Reject executable model-supplied validation commands
codex_findings.detail: For model-generated proposals, checking only the first token and a small metacharacter blacklist does not make a command read-only: inputs such as `make clean` or `python3 -m pytest /tmp/attacker.py` pass this filter, despite referring outside `allowed_paths` or executing arbitrary repository/Python code. These commands are hidden from the proposal card and later run with `shell=True` in `builder_attempt.run_validation`, so prompt injection or malformed model output can execute unintended host commands after an otherwise legitimate approval; either derive commands deterministically or parse and enforce command-specific path/argument constraints.

codex_findings.title: Require Mission identity before approving Builder work
codex_findings.detail: When a client omits `gateway_mission_id`, this condition skips every independent-review and Mission-state check and calls `mission_approve` directly. The HTTP schema also makes the field optional, so a caller with the prepared manifest, nonce, and `confirmed: true` can create the Builder job while the corresponding plan remains unreviewed, defeating the plan-review gate this change introduces. Require the Mission identity on this approval surface rather than preserving the ungated path.

codex_findings.title: Restore the persisted draft before showing approval
codex_findings.detail: On a chat reload, the version-3 checkpoint contains the exact edited `task` that produced the stored prepared manifest, but this hydration effect restores only the identities and proposal, leaving `draft` initialized from the original immutable chat message. If the user edited the objective, instructions, or allowed paths before compiling, the reloaded card displays the old values while `doApprove` submits the edited `prepared_manifest`, so the user can confirm work different from the proposal shown on screen. Restore `stored.task` into `draft` whenever a prepared or pending checkpoint is loaded.

codex_findings.title: Reconcile Mission binding before clearing recovery state
codex_findings.detail: When Builder accepts a job but the subsequent Gateway Mission binding fails, this branch preserves the approval checkpoint, but on reload the existing recovery effect clears that checkpoint as soon as `resumeBuilderJob` finds the Builder initiative. It never replays the nonce-bound approval to retry `bind_builder_locator`/`begin_execution`, so the UI presents the Builder job as recovered while the Gateway Mission remains in `PLAN_REVIEW` with no task locator; recovery must confirm or repair the Mission binding before discarding the checkpoint.

codex_findings.title: Make rejected proposals revisable or actually retry review
codex_findings.detail: After a reviewer rejects a plan, `record_plan_review` leaves the Mission in `PLANNING` with `review_state == 'rejected'`, but this button calls `doPropose` with the same persisted initiative and unchanged draft. The deterministic planning artifacts and digest are therefore identical, so `set_plan` returns early without restoring `PLAN_REVIEW/unreviewed`, and the background request returns `not_pending`; because the card also no longer exposes its Edit control once `proposal` exists, the visible “Retry review” action is a no-op and the user cannot recover from rejection in place.

codex_findings.title: Freeze the Mission plan once Builder work is bound
codex_findings.detail: This permits `set_plan` to replace the plan while the Mission is already `EXECUTING`; it only excludes `STOPPED` and `DONE`. Re-proposing the same initiative with changed instructions after approval therefore resets the Gateway Mission to `PLAN_REVIEW` and binds a new digest while its immutable Builder initiative/task still executes the old manifest. A later approval cannot apply the conflicting manifest, leaving the two durable authorities permanently inconsistent; reject plan replacement once a task locator is bound or require a new Mission identity.

codex_findings.title: Gate the paid reviewer as paid execution
codex_findings.detail: This action is registered as automatically executable T0 work with no authoritative cost estimate, but its implementation invokes the paid `openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-flash` route. With an OpenRouter key configured, proposal dispatch and startup recovery can therefore spend money without a spend grant, compute-governor check, or reconciliation—and repeated pending-plan recoveries can repeat that spend. Route this through the paid-execution authorization and budget authority instead of T0.

codex_findings.title: Propagate Mission lifecycle controls to Builder
codex_findings.detail: For an `EXECUTING` Mission with a bound Builder initiative, this endpoint only changes the Gateway Mission row to `PAUSED`; it never invokes Builder's supported `execution_pause`/initiative pause authority, so the queued or running Builder work continues while the API reports the Mission paused. Resume and stop have the same split-brain behavior, with stop leaving the Builder task able to finish or publish after the user asked to stop it. Coordinate these controls through the stored locator and Builder's canonical commands before reporting the Mission transition.

codex_findings.title: Add clean trigger phrases to every specialist skill
codex_findings.detail: Direct specialist requests using the leading advertised phrases are not discoverable because `_triggers()` preserves scaffolding such as `the user wants to`; for example, `suggest("harden code")`, `suggest("improve architecture")`, `suggest("verify a test is real")`, and `suggest("improve day-to-day experience")` all return no specialist.
