codex_findings.title: Resolve glossary includes before injecting skill prompts
codex_findings.detail: This remains an inert shell directive when a skill is loaded through Kitty: `gateway/skill_registry.py`'s `invoke()` only strips frontmatter and returns the Markdown verbatim, so it neither executes `cat` nor defines `COMMANDCODE_SKILL_DIR`. The same directive was added to the three new specialist skills, meaning agents receive the placeholder rather than the canonical `LANGUAGE.md` content even though each skill requires that exact vocabulary; inline the glossary or add a bounded relative-include expansion to the loader.

codex_findings.title: Expose the router phrases to the trigger matcher
codex_findings.detail: The new router is not selected for any of the six requests advertised here. `gateway/skill_registry.py` extracts everything after `Use when`, splits on commas, and performs literal substring matching without removing quotes or scaffolding such as `the user says`; consequently `skill_registry.suggest()` returns `[]` for `improve the codebase`, `make this better`, `what should I fix`, `review the quality`, `harden this`, and `clean this up`. Put clean, unquoted trigger phrases in `when_to_use` or otherwise format the description for the existing matcher so the router can fulfill its entry-point role.

codex_findings.title: Validate the whole installed session-end bundle
codex_findings.detail: When `session-end` is installed in one of the standalone locations supported by `gateway/session_end_audit.py`, copying only the changed `SKILL.md` makes `_installed_skill_findings()` report a matching, valid installation even if this new `references/receipt-schema.md` file was not copied. The installed prompt then cannot load the required receipt fields or commands, so the closeout workflow that owns the KB receipt is incomplete despite passing its audit; either keep the required schema inline or make installation/auditing validate the referenced bundle.

codex_findings.title: Add a UUID fallback for remote HTTP clients
codex_findings.detail: When Kitty is launched with `KITTY_UI_BIND_ALL=true` and opened from another device over `http://<LAN-or-Tailnet-IP>:4000`—a mode explicitly supported by `scripts/desktop/start_ui.sh`—the origin is not a secure context, so browsers do not expose `crypto.randomUUID()`. This call runs while `KittyProvider` initializes its first chat, causing the entire UI to throw before rendering; use the existing `getRandomValues` fallback pattern from `BuilderProposalCard` or another collision-resistant fallback.

codex_findings.title: Rebuild when the public initials setting changes
codex_findings.detail: When an existing installation adds or changes `NEXT_PUBLIC_KITTY_USER_EMAIL` in the documented root `.env`, restarting Kitty continues to show the initials compiled into the previous bundle. The bundled Next 16 guide states that `NEXT_PUBLIC_` references are inlined by `next build` and frozen afterward, while `scripts/desktop/start_ui.sh` only rebuilds for newer inputs under `gateway/kitty-chat` and does not include the root `.env`; it therefore reports the build as current and serves the stale value. Include this setting in build invalidation or obtain the initials through a runtime configuration path.

codex_findings.title: Enforce the LiteLLM pin in launcher preflight
codex_findings.detail: On an existing installation whose isolated LiteLLM environment contains an out-of-range version such as 1.90.x or 1.92.x, restarting after this change does not enforce the new `~=1.91.1` contract. `gateway/start_litellm.sh` parses this requirements file but validates only the installed `openai` version plus one LiteLLM constant, so such an environment still passes preflight and never enters the auto-repair path; validate `md.version("litellm")` against the declared LiteLLM specifier as well.

codex_findings.title: Abort invocation when a required include is unavailable
codex_findings.detail: When a skill bundle is copied without `LANGUAGE.md`, or the file is unreadable or oversized, the new expander returns a blockquote and `invoke()` still reports success; `gateway/context_assembler.py` consequently accepts the prompt as usable and runs the specialist without its required glossary. Raise an error here so incomplete bundles cannot silently degrade an invoked skill.

codex_findings.title: Abort invocation when a required include cannot be loaded
codex_findings.detail: When an installed skill bundle omits `LANGUAGE.md` (or the file is unreadable/oversized), this new expansion path substitutes a blockquote and still returns a successful invocation, so `context_assembler._default_skill_hint()` accepts an incomplete prompt as usable instructions. Raise an invocation error instead of silently running a specialist without its required glossary.

codex_findings.title: Rebuild when the root environment file is removed
codex_findings.detail: When an existing installation deletes its root `.env` after building—for example, to restore the documented `JB` fallback—this guard omits the now-absent file from `build_inputs`, so the launcher declares the build current and keeps serving the old inlined initials. I reproduced this with the launcher fixture, and the bundled Next 16 environment guide confirms that `NEXT_PUBLIC_` values remain frozen after `next build`; persist enough state to detect file removal as well as a newer file.

codex_findings.title: Rebuild when the root environment file is removed
codex_findings.detail: When the root `.env` is deleted after a bundle was built with `NEXT_PUBLIC_KITTY_USER_EMAIL`, this conditional drops the file from `build_inputs`, so the launcher declares the old bundle current and continues showing the former initials instead of the documented fallback. The bundled Next 16 environment guide confirms that public values remain frozen after `next build`; preserve enough build metadata to detect removal as well as newer-file edits.

review_units.title: fix(runtime): converge personal workspace and serving stack
review_units.head: 1b1c1ad2d8b3f04ef150ec7e0c45853f3a838ee8

codex_findings.title: Record the listener's startup revision
codex_findings.detail: If either worktree advances after its listener starts, this reads the worktree's current `HEAD`, not the revision loaded by the running process. UI and Gateway listeners from different startup revisions can consequently receive the same new identity, causing `kitty status` to report a coherent stack that is “serving this exact checkout/source” while one process still serves old code. Persist or inspect startup/build provenance rather than deriving process identity from mutable checkout state.

codex_findings.title: Distinguish a stopped stack from a partial one
codex_findings.detail: When neither the UI nor Gateway is listening, both identities are empty and this branch still returns `partial`; consequently `kitty status` describes a completely stopped product as a partially serving stack. Handle the both-empty case first and report an explicit stopped/absent state so the operator-facing runtime summary does not invent availability.

codex_findings.title: Record provenance for launchd-started listeners
codex_findings.detail: The normal `kitty install` path launches `gateway/start_gateway.sh` and `scripts/desktop/start_ui.sh` directly from `scripts/kitty_desktop_launchd.py`, so neither process ever calls `record_runtime_identity`; a sibling worktree's record is likewise stored under that worktree's own `RUN_DIR`. In both cases this current-directory-only lookup returns no identities for healthy Kitty-owned listeners, and `kitty status` consequently reports the installed stack as `partial` with `external/unknown` components. Persist provenance where all worktrees and launchd-managed services can supply it.

codex_findings.title: Match runtime identities to the requested service
codex_findings.detail: After an unclean shutdown or reboot leaves identity files behind, a new listener can reuse the PID recorded for a different service. Because this loop accepts the first of `ui.identity`, `gateway.identity`, or `litellm.identity` with that PID, a newly started Gateway can be assigned a stale UI revision even though its current `gateway.identity` is present, causing `kitty status` to report a false split or stale checkout; look up only the identity file for the service being classified, or include a process-start token that prevents PID reuse matches.

codex_findings.title: Expand user-relative data-root overrides
codex_findings.detail: When `KITTY_DATA_ROOT` uses the supported `~/...` form, `gateway.paths.DATA_DIR` expands it but this resolver retains the literal tilde. `require_existing_personal_workspace` therefore rejects `~/kitty-data` as missing even when `$HOME/kitty-data` exists, so previously valid overrides can no longer start Kitty. Expand and normalize the override before checking it or deriving the Builder and governor paths.

codex_findings.title: Normalize relative workspace roots before launching subprocesses
codex_findings.detail: When `KITTY_DATA_ROOT` is relative and `kitty` is invoked outside the checkout, this guard resolves the path against the caller's directory, but `gateway/start_gateway.sh` later changes directory to `KITTY_ROOT` before Python interprets the same relative value; `kitty builder` and backup commands do not make that directory change. A valid `KITTY_DATA_ROOT=store` can therefore pass the existence check and silently send Gateway and Builder to different stores. Convert the selected root to one absolute path before deriving and exporting the three workspace variables.

codex_findings.title: Require the personal database before accepting the workspace
codex_findings.detail: When an implicit data root contains only `kittybuilder/builder_queue.db` or `compute_governor/receipts.db`—for example after restoring ancillary state without the personal database—this any-of check passes and Gateway can start with a newly created empty `kitty/kitty.db`, presenting missing personal history as a valid workspace. Fresh evidence in this revision is the new marker loop treating support-state databases as proof that the personal store exists; require the canonical personal database rather than accepting any subsystem marker.

codex_findings.title: Validate that the default workspace contains personal data
codex_findings.detail: In a fresh clone or unrelated standalone checkout, the repository's tracked `data/.gitkeep` means this directory test succeeds even though no personal workspace exists. `cmd_up` then starts against fresh empty stores and presents missing history as a valid workspace—the exact scenario this guard claims to reject. Check for substantive canonical state, while preserving an explicit path for intentional first-run or sandbox initialization.

codex_findings.title: Include dirty state in the current runtime identity
codex_findings.detail: When the stack is started from a dirty checkout, `runtime_source_sha` deliberately records both listeners as `$KITTY_ROOT@dirty:$sha`, but this comparison constructs `$KITTY_ROOT@$sha` without the dirty prefix. Even with both components coherently serving the unchanged dirty source they started from, `kitty status` therefore claims they are serving a different checkout/source. Build `current_identity` with the same helper or normalization used for the startup record.

codex_findings.title: Expand nested overrides before reporting workspace conflicts
codex_findings.detail: Although the runtime resolver now expands user-relative overrides, the read-only status path compares the literal `KITTY_BUILDER_DATA_DIR`. With `KITTY_DATA_ROOT=~/kitty-data` and the valid matching override `KITTY_BUILDER_DATA_DIR=~/kitty-data/kittybuilder`, startup accepts the configuration after expansion but `kitty status` reports a conflict; the governor comparison has the same mismatch. Apply `expand_user_path` consistently before producing the conflict report.

codex_findings.title: Keep Agent Room independent of governor overrides
codex_findings.detail: When an isolated worktree sets `KITTY_COMPUTE_GOVERNOR_DB` independently from `KITTY_DATA_ROOT`—the supported isolation case documented by `gateway/compute_governor.py`—every `./kitty room` command now exits in this coherence helper before the Room CLI runs. Agent Room only needs canonical `KITTY_DATA_ROOT`; use a data-root-only resolver here so an unrelated governor override cannot block mandatory inbox and handoff access.

codex_findings.title: Keep restore drills independent of live workspace overrides
codex_findings.detail: When the environment intentionally isolates `KITTY_BUILDER_DATA_DIR` or `KITTY_COMPUTE_GOVERNOR_DB` from `KITTY_DATA_ROOT`, `restore-drill` now exits in the coherence resolver before inspecting or copying the supplied archive. A restore drill only copies `BACKUP_DIR` into the new `RESTORE_DIR` and never accesses the selected live workspace, so this guard prevents the documented non-destructive verification operation for otherwise supported isolated environments; invoke the drill directly without runtime workspace resolution.

codex_findings.title: Restore the canonical data root for agent commands
codex_findings.detail: When `./kitty agent` runs from a linked worktree without an explicit `KITTY_DATA_ROOT`, removing this canonicalization leaves `gateway.paths.KITTY_DB_FILE` bound to that worktree's local `data/kitty/kitty.db`. The ownership mutex remains in the canonical `.kitty-coordination.db`, but `_project_event` reports success after writing claim, conflict, and release events into the private Room database, so other worktrees do not see those coordination events; use the data-root-only resolver already used by `cmd_room`.

codex_findings.title: Derive owner backups from the actual data root
codex_findings.detail: When `KITTY_DATA_ROOT` is a supported arbitrary directory such as `/tmp/isolated-data`, this changes the owner root to `/tmp` while the inventory still looks under `data/kitty`; the real `/tmp/isolated-data/kitty` is therefore recorded as missing and the command exits successfully with an empty or incomplete backup. Default restore has the symmetric problem and writes under `/tmp/data` rather than the selected root. Map data-relative entries directly from `DATA_DIR` instead of assuming every override is named `data`.

codex_findings.title: Keep configuration backups anchored to the runtime checkout
codex_findings.detail: When `KITTY_DATA_ROOT` is a conventional external path ending in `data`, such as `/tmp/profile/data`, this chooses `/tmp/profile` as the project root. `_owner_path` then backs up and restores `config/...` under `/tmp/profile`, even though `gateway.paths.CONFIG_DIR` and the running application still read configuration from the source checkout's `ROOT/config`. The default backup therefore records the real preferences and profile as missing while succeeding, and restore writes them where Kitty never reads them. Keep non-data inventory paths anchored to `ROOT` while mapping only `data/...` through `DATA_DIR`.

codex_findings.title: Quiesce Builder before replacing its queue database
codex_findings.detail: When an owner-data archive is restored with `--replace` while a Builder supervisor or worker is active, this newly included database is moved aside and recreated without stopping its users; any open connection and `builder_queue.db-wal`/`-shm` sidecars remain at the original location, so concurrent writes or WAL replay can corrupt the restored queue or silently discard newer initiative state. Refuse the restore until Builder is quiescent, or checkpoint and replace the complete SQLite store atomically.

codex_findings.title: Quiesce the compute-governor store before replacing it
codex_findings.detail: When an owner-data archive is restored with `--replace` while a Builder supervisor or reviewer is recording governed work, the newly included `data/compute_governor` directory is moved and replaced without any preflight for that live WAL database. Existing connections can continue writing through handles to the moved-aside files while subsequent connections use the restored database, silently splitting or losing the authoritative receipt history; stop the writers or checkpoint and replace this SQLite store under the same preflight as the Builder queue.

codex_findings.title: Detect detached Builder supervisors before restore
codex_findings.detail: When a task is running through `run_worker_detached`, its process command is `python -m gateway.builder_runner --supervise ...` (see `gateway/builder_runner.py`), which matches none of these markers, so the new quiescence check can declare Builder inactive and replace its live queue database. Fresh evidence after the earlier review is that the added process scanner omits this repository's actual detached-worker argv; include that process or query Builder's supported active-run state before replacement.

codex_findings.title: Reject backups without the canonical personal database
codex_findings.detail: When the selected `KITTY_DATA_ROOT` is missing or empty, this path is accepted without validation; the backup command creates its destination, records `data/kitty` and every other data store as missing, copies only checkout configuration, and exits successfully. A mistyped override can therefore produce an archive that appears successful but contains no personal history, so require `data/kitty/kitty.db` before publishing an owner-data backup rather than treating that store as optional.

codex_findings.title: Check Builder quiescence before moving any live data
codex_findings.detail: When `--replace` is used while a recognized Builder process is active, the restore moves and replaces earlier inventory entries such as `data/kitty` before reaching this queue-specific check. The subsequent refusal enters the exception cleanup, which deletes the newly restored paths but does not move their originals back, so a command that reports it refused the restore leaves the live personal-data paths absent under `.pre-restore-*`; perform the Builder preflight before the restore loop mutates any destination.

review_units.title: fix(work): stop reporting Builder's finished task as a finished outcome
review_units.head: de69cd2a92795a5b0fd0cef78a62ea5839dab694

codex_findings.title: Keep active sequencing in the sole roadmap
codex_findings.detail: This new design document establishes a live execution order and ownership rule for unfinished P3/P4 work, creating a second active delivery backlog outside `docs/ROADMAP.md`; it is already stale within this commit because P3-A is still labeled “not started.” Move the active statuses and sequence into the canonical roadmap, or make this document explicitly historical/non-authoritative so future agents do not follow conflicting delivery state.

codex_findings.title: Surface Mission-store outages while work is running
codex_findings.detail: When `/builder/conversation/resume` reports `mission_acceptance.state === 'unavailable'` for a running Builder task, `_awaiting_acceptance()` returns false because Builder is not done yet, so this branch applies the green success styling and the acceptance warning below is not rendered. The user therefore sees no indication that the durable Mission evidence is missing or unreadable until the task reaches `done`; treat an unavailable acceptance store as an attention/degraded state independently of `awaiting_acceptance` and display its cause immediately.

codex_findings.title: Keep unaccepted outcomes out of the success state
codex_findings.detail: When Builder is done but Mission acceptance is `unreviewed`, `rejected`, or unavailable, this newly added message is rendered inside the card's green `successBox`. The text therefore warns that the outcome is not accepted while the surrounding visual state still signals success—the same false completion cue this change is meant to remove; render awaiting acceptance as a warning/attention state and reserve the success styling for accepted outcomes.

codex_findings.title: Surface the Mission-store failure cause
codex_findings.detail: When the Mission database is missing, locked, or corrupt, the backend now preserves the actual cause in `mission_acceptance.error`, but this branch collapses every such failure to the same generic sentence and never renders that field. Fresh evidence after the earlier backend finding is that the error reaches `ConversationResume` but is discarded here, making distinct outages indistinguishable and leaving no specific repair guidance; show a safe, actionable form of the reported cause.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the read-only contract for result polling
codex_findings.detail: Every `work_result()` call with an initiative now reaches this `init_db()`, which executes `CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE`, and `CREATE INDEX` statements. That makes the MCP read/recovery tool mutate and potentially lock the application database merely while polling results; on a read-only database it also prevents acceptance from being read. Query the existing schema without initialization and report the schema/store as unavailable when it is absent.

codex_findings.title: Open the Mission database in read-only mode
codex_findings.detail: When the Mission DB path does not exist, this supposedly read-only lookup still calls `gateway.db.connect()`, which creates the parent directory, database, and WAL/SHM files before the query raises `MissionError`; it can also apply `journal_mode=WAL` to an existing database. Fresh evidence after the earlier review is that replacing `init_db()` with this connection removed schema creation but not filesystem/database mutation, so use a true SQLite read-only connection or reject a missing path before connecting.

codex_findings.title: Escape the database path before building the SQLite URI
codex_findings.detail: When `MISSION_DB_FILE` or an explicit `db_path` has a valid URI-reserved character such as `?` or `#` anywhere in its path, interpolating it directly into this URI makes SQLite treat the remainder as a query or fragment instead of part of the filename. The lookup then opens the wrong database and may even create a truncated-path file because `mode=ro` is no longer parsed, so configured or isolated stores under such directories always report unavailable and violate the read-only contract; construct the URI from a percent-encoded file URI before appending `mode=ro`.

codex_findings.title: Prevent result polls from recreating SQLite sidecars
codex_findings.detail: When the existing Mission database is in WAL mode—as configured by every `kitty_db.connect()` writer—opening this `mode=ro` URI and executing the lookup can still create persistent `kitty.db-wal` and `kitty.db-shm` files if those sidecars are absent. Fresh runtime evidence against the current read-only fix is that a WAL database containing only its main file gains both sidecars immediately after this exact read-only `SELECT`; polling therefore still mutates the filesystem and can fail when the database directory is genuinely read-only. Use a snapshot/checkpoint or another connection strategy that guarantees the lookup cannot create SQLite sidecars while still reading current committed data.

codex_findings.title: Avoid loading every Mission on each poll
codex_findings.detail: `useResumeBuilderJob` refetches every 10 seconds for each mounted job card, but this lookup executes `SELECT *` over every bound Mission, materializes all potentially large plan/checkpoint/evidence JSON columns, and then parses rows in Python merely to find one initiative. As Mission and chat history grow, multiple cards cause repeated O(cards × missions) database reads and deserialization while Chat is idle; filter by the initiative in SQLite, preferably through an indexed normalized/JSON locator with `LIMIT 1`, and hydrate only the matching row.

codex_findings.title: Avoid loading every Mission on each poll
codex_findings.detail: `useResumeBuilderJob` refetches every 10 seconds for each mounted job card, but this lookup executes `SELECT *` over every bound Mission, materializes all potentially large plan/checkpoint/evidence JSON, and then parses rows in Python just to find one initiative. As Mission and chat history grows, multiple cards produce repeated O(cards × Missions) database reads and deserialization while Chat is idle; filter by initiative in SQLite—ideally through an indexed normalized locator or `json_extract`—use `LIMIT 1`, and hydrate only the matching row.

codex_findings.title: Surface Mission-store failures instead of swallowing them
codex_findings.detail: When the Mission database is locked, corrupt, permission-denied, or otherwise unreadable, this broad handler discards the exception and returns the same value used for a genuinely unbound initiative; the enclosing receipt then still reports `ok: true` and misleadingly says no acceptance record exists. Preserve the Builder evidence if desired, but expose an unavailable/error state with the actual cause so callers can repair the store rather than treating an outage as missing data.

codex_findings.title: Read acceptance from the configured Mission store
codex_findings.detail: When the application or an isolated test overrides `memory_mission.MISSION_DB_FILE` after module import, Mission writes use that current module value, but this call omits `db_path` and therefore uses the function's definition-time default pointing at the canonical database. The resulting receipt can report `none` or `unavailable` for a Mission that exists in the configured store, and isolated tests can unexpectedly access the real database; pass `memory_mission.MISSION_DB_FILE` explicitly as the writers and routes already do.

codex_findings.title: Treat an absent Mission store as unbound for direct MCP work
codex_findings.detail: When Builder MCP is used before the Gateway Mission database or `missions` table has ever been initialized, a direct completed job reaches this lookup, the resulting `MissionError` is converted to `mission_acceptance.state: "unavailable"`, and `_awaiting_acceptance()` consequently reports that the job is waiting for acceptance even though acceptance does not apply to direct Builder work. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier completion-gate issue is that `complete` now remains true but the new adjacent acceptance fields still falsely report an open gate in this supported standalone context; when `expect_binding` is false, distinguish an uninitialized Mission store from an unreadable existing store and return `none` for the former.

codex_findings.title: Keep completion reachable through production workflows
codex_findings.detail: Once a Builder task finishes through either the documented MCP `mission_prepare`/`mission_approve` flow or the conversation handoff, this new gate can remain false forever: direct MCP approval never creates or binds a Gateway Mission, and a repo-wide search finds no production caller of `record_candidate()` or `record_acceptance()` to transition a conversation Mission to `accepted`. Consequently, ordinary completed jobs report `complete: false` with no supported action capable of satisfying this condition; add the missing production acceptance lifecycle or avoid applying this gate to workflows that cannot record acceptance.

codex_findings.title: Apply the acceptance gate to the Chat resume projection
codex_findings.detail: When a conversation-backed job is reopened—the user-facing scenario this commit claims to repair—the UI calls `/builder/conversation/resume`, which delegates to `_context.resume_context`; that projection still returns only Builder `mission.state` and `current_work.state`, never calls `work_result()`, and never includes these new acceptance fields. Therefore this change only affects direct MCP `work_result` callers and cannot stop Kitty Chat from presenting Builder's terminal state as the finished user outcome; thread Mission acceptance through the resume projection and its consumer.

codex_findings.title: Treat missing Mission bindings as unknown in Chat
codex_findings.detail: When a conversation-backed Builder job survives but its Gateway Mission row or locator does not—for example after restoring or migrating the two stores independently—`mission_for_initiative()` returns `None`, this branch clears `awaiting_acceptance`, and `ResumedBuilderJob` renders the completed job in the green success state with no acceptance warning. That contradicts the lookup contract that `None` means unknown and hides the missing outcome evidence; distinguish direct MCP work where acceptance is genuinely not applicable from a conversation job whose expected Mission binding is absent, and surface the latter as unavailable/attention.

codex_findings.title: Preserve task completion through cold-start errors
codex_findings.detail: When `resume_context(task_id=...)` reopens a done packet in an initiative that still has other work, any unrelated failed Kitty context check first replaces `state` with `attention`; this expression then reports `builder_task_complete: false` and suppresses `awaiting_acceptance`, even though the same receipt's `current_work.state` remains `done`. Compute packet completion directly from `current.task_state` rather than from the overwritten presentation state so the supported Builder projection does not contradict itself.

codex_findings.title: Render acceptance state in the resumed chat card
codex_findings.detail: For a conversation-backed job whose Builder initiative is completed while its Mission remains unreviewed or unavailable, these new fields do not change what the user sees: `ConversationResume` does not declare them and `ResumedBuilderJob` still renders only `mission.state` and `current_work.state`, so Chat continues to show “completed”/“done” without the open acceptance gate. Fresh evidence in this revision is that `resume_context()` now returns the acceptance fields, but no consumer was added for them; thread them through the response type and render the pending/unavailable state.

review_units.title: feat(projects): let a project point at the action you actually chose
review_units.head: a42f73653badf534f4fda39e2c5c91ccfa1f7bc4

codex_findings.title: Reject todos owned by another project
codex_findings.detail: When a todo already has `project_id = B`, calling `select_todo(A, todo_id)` succeeds because this check considers only global ID existence. The project then points at a selected todo whose own durable association names a different project, giving callers contradictory ownership; reject such mismatches or atomically reassign the todo before storing the pointer.

codex_findings.title: Reject deprioritized todos as selected actions
codex_findings.detail: The distinct uncovered status case is `deprioritized`: this guard rejects only `completed`, so an already-deprioritized todo can be selected and returned as the project's next action. `todo_store.get_todos_text()` treats only `pending` and `in_progress` as active, confirming that deprioritized items are not actionable; restrict selections to those active statuses and revalidate the same invariant when reading them.

codex_findings.title: Make todo adoption and selection atomic
codex_findings.detail: When selecting an unowned todo, this call commits the ownership change before the project pointer is written through a separate connection. If the subsequent project update fails—for example because SQLite becomes locked or the write encounters an I/O error—the endpoint returns an error but leaves the todo adopted by the project without any selection; perform both writes in one transaction or roll back the adoption on failure.

codex_findings.title: Claim unowned todos conditionally
codex_findings.detail: When ownership requests overlap, `owner` is read before this transaction, so another request can assign the todo after validation and this unconditional update will silently steal it and leave the other project's pointer inconsistent. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier ownership comment is that the squashed revision still updates by `id` alone; claim ownership with `WHERE id = ? AND project_id IS NULL` inside the transaction and reject a zero-row update.

codex_findings.title: Stop returning completed todos as the chosen next action
codex_findings.detail: After the selected todo is completed through the existing completion endpoint, its row still exists, so this loop continues returning it indefinitely. Because this endpoint represents the action that should outrank generated suggestions, callers can keep presenting already completed work as the project's next action; completion should clear the selection, or this lookup should reject non-actionable statuses.

codex_findings.title: Preserve selected todos when regenerated lists omit them
codex_findings.detail: When a regenerated `POST /todos` payload omits the chosen item, `todo_store.update()` deletes that row and this fallback silently clears `selected_todo_id`. Generated suggestions can therefore erase the explicit user choice that this commit is intended to preserve, while a read request hides the loss by rewriting durable state and returning `None`; preserve referenced todos or make removal explicit and observable instead.

codex_findings.title: Revalidate ownership when returning the selected todo
codex_findings.detail: Fresh evidence after the earlier ownership finding is the still-writable `/todos/{todo_id}/project` path in `gateway/routes/extended.py`: after project A selects an unowned todo, that endpoint can assign it to project B, but this loop continues returning it as A's selection without checking `project_id`. The durable pointer and todo ownership then contradict each other, so enforce the invariant during reassignment or reject/clear mismatches here.

codex_findings.title: Clear selections when a todo becomes unowned
codex_findings.detail: Fresh evidence beyond the earlier cross-project reassignment case is that `/todos/{todo_id}/project` accepts `project_id: null`, but this check still treats `owner is None` as valid. After explicitly removing a selected todo's project association, project A therefore continues returning that unowned todo as its chosen project action; require `owner == project_id` for an existing selection or clear it during unassignment.

codex_findings.title: Clear only the selection that was validated
codex_findings.detail: When a GET overlaps a new PUT selection, this read may load the old `selected_todo_id`, decide that old todo is invalid, and then `clear_selected_todo()` unconditionally erase the newer choice committed by the PUT. Make the repair a conditional update such as `WHERE id = ? AND selected_todo_id = ?`, so a read cannot silently discard a concurrent explicit user choice.

codex_findings.title: Refuse split stores before repairing the selection
codex_findings.detail: When `TODO_DB_FILE` and `PROJECTS_DB_FILE` are independently redirected, this lookup reads the non-authoritative todo database even though the new write paths explicitly reject that configuration. If the selected ID is absent there, the following repair silently clears the valid pointer in the project database; if the same ID exists, it can return an unrelated todo. Apply the same resolved-path guard here and raise instead of mutating state from unavailable evidence.

codex_findings.title: Reject boolean todo IDs before selection
codex_findings.detail: When the request body contains `{"todo_id": true}`, Pydantic coerces the boolean to integer `1` before `select_todo()` runs, so the store's explicit boolean guard never sees it; if todo 1 exists, the endpoint returns 200 and changes the user's selection to that unrelated item. Declare this field as `StrictInt` or otherwise enable strict integer validation so malformed JSON receives a 422 instead of mutating durable state.

codex_findings.title: Protect selections inside the todo transaction
codex_findings.detail: When a `PUT /projects/{id}/selected-todo` overlaps `POST /todos`, the update can snapshot `protected` before the PUT commits, then delete the newly selected omitted todo after the PUT returns. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier regeneration finding is that the final fix deliberately reads protections outside the todo transaction, leaving a dangling pointer and silently losing the chosen action; initialize the stores first, then read selections and reconcile under one database transaction or otherwise revalidate before deletion.

codex_findings.title: Avoid initializing projects inside the todo write transaction
codex_findings.detail: On a fresh database where the project seed settings do not exist, a non-empty first `POST /todos` has already inserted or updated rows on the outer SQLite connection before this call. `list_projects()` runs `project_store.init_db()` and tries to seed projects through a second connection; that writer waits for the configured five-second busy timeout and raises `database is locked`, so the first update stalls before the catch below masks the failure. Load selections before beginning the todo write transaction or read them through the existing connection.

codex_findings.title: Abort reconciliation when selections cannot be loaded
codex_findings.detail: When the projects database is locked, corrupt, or otherwise unreadable during `POST /todos`, this broad catch treats the failure as “no protected todos”; the `dropped` calculation then deletes every omitted selected todo and commits successfully, leaving dangling project pointers and lost progress. Propagate the lookup error so reconciliation cannot destructively continue without its protection evidence.

codex_findings.title: Separate snapshot restoration from generated-list reconciliation
codex_findings.detail: When `storage_sync.import_all()` restores a snapshot whose `todos` omit a currently selected row, `import_todos()` delegates to this `update()` function, so the protected row survives even though the import contract says it replaces the store. The restored database therefore contains stale current-state data that was not present in the backup; use an explicit reconciliation mode for generated suggestions versus snapshot restoration, or clear/reconcile selections during import.

codex_findings.title: Assign protected todos a unique sort position
codex_findings.detail: When regeneration omits a selected todo, this preserves its old `sort_order` while assigning incoming items positions starting at zero. If the selected todo was previously at one of those positions, the resulting rows have duplicate positions; ordering becomes ambiguous, and the public `todo_store.complete(index)` updates every row sharing that position. Move protected omitted rows to unique positions after the regenerated list or renumber the complete result.

codex_findings.title: Reject duplicate sort positions during restore
codex_findings.detail: When `/sync/import` receives a hand-edited or legacy snapshot containing two integer `sort_order` values that are equal, this branch preserves both positions instead of assigning unique positions as the previous import path did. The public `todo_store.complete(index)` updates every row matching that position, so completing either imported item silently marks both completed. Validate position uniqueness and reject the snapshot before replacing the store.

codex_findings.title: Reject dangling project owners during restore
codex_findings.detail: When `/sync/import` restores a snapshot into a fresh database, a todo may carry the source database's user-created `project_id`, but projects are not included in this snapshot. This branch accepts any integer without checking that the project exists, and there is no foreign key on `todos.project_id`, so the import succeeds with a dangling owner; subsequent attempts to select that todo for a real project are rejected as belonging to the nonexistent ID. Refuse the restore when its referenced projects are unavailable rather than committing an unusable association.

review_units.title: fix(runtime): recognize managed LiteLLM listener child
review_units.head: 4451fabd9c35b9f94cc56d727dd0d8c6821a4bf6

codex_findings.title: Fence controller PID reuse before assigning ownership
codex_findings.detail: After an unclean shutdown leaves a service pidfile, its numeric PID can be recycled by an unrelated process running from this checkout; if that process happens to have the listener as a direct child, this helper accepts it without verifying the controller command, service identity, or recorded process start identity. `cmd_status` then upgrades an otherwise unknown listener to `owned-current` and suppresses the metadata mismatch even though the pidfile is stale. Bind the pidfile to a service-specific process identity rather than trusting PID, cwd, and parentage alone.

codex_findings.title: Apply managed-child ownership in every status section
codex_findings.detail: When the LiteLLM listener is a direct child whose cwd is the isolated venv—the exact scenario handled here—this override affects only the first service summary. The later `Listeners` section recomputes `pid_role` directly, so `./kitty status` reports the same PID first as `owned-current` and later as `external`; I reproduced both lines with a managed child listener. Route both sections through the same controller-aware classification so the runtime report is internally consistent.

review_units.title: perf(dev): bound ordinary pre-push checks
review_units.head: 506fa4c9624b9ffc773a85e492469612f7c04747

codex_findings.title: Derive bounded checks from every pushed ref
codex_findings.detail: The installed Git pre-push documentation specifies that each stdin line contains `<local ref> <local oid> <remote ref> <remote oid>`, but this classifier derives `RUN_CODE` and `RUN_FRONTEND` solely from `origin/main...HEAD`. When `git push origin otherbranch` is run while a documentation-only branch is checked out, or when multiple refs are pushed, the hook can print “All clear” without testing the code candidate actually being published; classify each non-deletion `local_oid` from stdin and union their scopes instead.

codex_findings.title: Exclude deleted Python paths from bounded commands
codex_findings.detail: When a commit deletes any `.py` file, `git diff --name-only` still includes that now-absent path and this code adds it to `CHANGED_PYTHON_FILES`; Ruff then exits with `E902 No such file or directory`, and deleted test files also make pytest exit with “file or directory not found.” Consequently the hook blocks every normal Python-file deletion, so filter the diff to non-deleted paths (for example with `--diff-filter=ACMR`) or verify each path exists before passing it to the tools.

codex_findings.title: Run full parity checks for documentation-only candidates
codex_findings.detail: When `--full` is used on a documentation-only candidate and `origin/main` exists, `RUN_CODE` is zero and this early return bypasses Ruff, mypy, and the entire pytest suite before reporting “All clear.” That contradicts the advertised offline/local-parity behavior and misses documentation-authority tests specifically affected by Markdown changes; full mode should keep the global Python gates unconditional, while only the frontend gates remain scope-dependent.

codex_findings.title: Preserve the lease-expiry assertion in the heartbeat test
codex_findings.detail: With `lease_seconds=30` and the child exiting as soon as a renewal call is observed, the run always finishes before its initial lease can expire. The test therefore passes even if `renew_lease` returns without extending `lease_expires_at`, so it no longer guards the behavior its name claims; retain the event-based synchronization while either keeping the worker alive past the original expiry or asserting that the persisted expiry actually advances.

review_units.title: test(builder): compare validation interpreter identity
review_units.head: 9eaf600b1fbd61fb0d5f63452acb9c5520ac1b34

codex_findings.title: Keep the test sensitive to virtual-environment activation
codex_findings.detail: When the repository environment was created with `venv`, its `bin/python` commonly resolves to the same base interpreter as the system `python`, even though only the former loads the repository environment. Consequently, removing the `PATH` prepend from `run_validation` can make the command select the base interpreter while this resolved-path comparison still passes; I reproduced exactly that case with a temporary venv. Compare environment identity such as `sys.prefix` instead so this remains a meaningful regression test.

review_units.title: fix(work): recover truthful resume and route state
review_units.head: ea692422def10a97900429ee6da95f67661a9b8a

codex_findings.title: Co-locate the project route with its regression tests
codex_findings.detail: This maps `tests/test_projects_routes.py` to `memory:continuity` while the same commit maps `gateway/routes/projects.py` to `ui:action-grammar`. A normal Builder fix that includes the route and its regression test therefore resolves to two resources, and `_planning_artifact_claim()` rejects the proposal because it requires exactly one resource, so Builder cannot prepare a properly tested change to this endpoint. Assign the route and its tests to the same semantic resource.

codex_findings.title: Return route metadata before consuming it
codex_findings.detail: For every successful production Work request, `conversation_handoff.compile_request()` returns `routing` but never the new `route` object (the existing backend test even asserts that `route` is absent), so this assignment always stores `null` and neither route/cost banner added by this commit can render. Return the actual provider/model/cost from `/builder/conversation/compile`, or handle its absence explicitly rather than silently hiding the promised evidence.

codex_findings.title: Preserve checkpoints through all Mission-store outages
codex_findings.detail: When Builder accepted the job but binding failed, resume can find the Builder initiative while `mission_for_initiative()` reports `unavailable` for an unreadable or rapidly changing Mission store rather than an error matching “binding missing.” This `!bindingMissing` condition then deletes the exact nonce-bound approval checkpoint even though a matching task binding was never confirmed; after the store recovers, the partial binding cannot be reconciled from this card. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier fix is that the current predicate treats every non-regex Mission outage as a resolved binding; retain the checkpoint until the receipt positively proves the expected task binding.

codex_findings.title: Retain the checkpoint after repeated binding failures
codex_findings.detail: When this newly added `bindingMissing` branch is shown, clicking **Retry same approval** can legitimately receive another HTTP-200 `{ok:false, error_code:'mission_binding_failed'}` receipt, such as while the Mission store remains locked. The invoked `retryPendingApproval` handler treats every `ok:false` result as final and deletes `localStorage`, `pendingApproval`, and `resumedMissionId`, losing the only exact nonce-bound payload after one failed reconciliation attempt. Fresh evidence in this revision is that the new `bindingMissing` branch now routes users into that unchanged destructive handler; preserve recovery-required receipts until resume confirms the binding.

codex_findings.title: Stop presenting the compile route as the execution route
codex_findings.detail: When a proposal does carry `draft.route`, it describes the model used by `/builder/conversation/compile`, but this prepared-state row labels it as the Builder execution route. Approval does not pass that route into the manifest, and the confirmation immediately below correctly says Builder chooses its execution route later under current policy, so users can be shown an unsupported provider/model and cost for the pending run. Keep this labeled as the proposal route until actual Builder preflight data is available.

codex_findings.title: Render rejected acceptance separately from pending
codex_findings.detail: When Mission acceptance is `rejected`, `_awaiting_acceptance()` deliberately returns true with a rejection reason, but this branch only distinguishes `unavailable`; every other state is rendered as “Nobody has accepted the result yet.” A completed Builder task whose outcome was explicitly rejected therefore looks merely pending and hides the repair decision from the user. Render `rejected` and its next action explicitly instead of collapsing it into the unreviewed message.

codex_findings.title: Preserve a retry for missing Mission bindings
codex_findings.detail: When Builder commits an approval but the Gateway Mission binding fails or the HTTP response is lost, reload restores the pending approval and finds the Builder initiative; the existing effect then clears that checkpoint solely because the Builder ID exists. The new unavailable-acceptance branch consequently tells the user to retry after the only exact approval payload and retry control have been discarded, leaving the missing binding unrecoverable from this card. Keep the checkpoint and expose `retryPendingApproval` until the resume receipt confirms a valid Mission binding.

codex_findings.title: Avoid copying the whole database on every resume poll
codex_findings.detail: Each approved proposal card uses `useResumeBuilderJob`, which polls every 10 seconds, and every poll reaches this code and copies the complete `kitty.db` plus its WAL. Because Chat renders every proposal card and the application database grows with unrelated personal data, a conversation containing multiple approved jobs causes multiple full-database copies every 10 seconds, blocking request workers, producing heavy disk I/O, and potentially reporting acceptance as unavailable when temporary storage is exhausted. Use a bounded read-only query or a shared/cached SQLite snapshot rather than copying the store once per initiative poll.

codex_findings.title: Require a task ID in expected Mission bindings
codex_findings.detail: When Builder commits the job but `bind_builder_locator(..., task_id=...)` fails, the Mission created during proposal already has a partial locator containing the initiative ID and a null task ID. This query treats that partial locator as a valid binding, so conversation resume reports `unreviewed` rather than `unavailable`; `missingMissionBinding` becomes false and the effect in `BuilderProposalCard.tsx` removes the only replayable approval checkpoint. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier fix is that the production lookup filters only by initiative ID and never verifies the current Builder task ID. Require the expected task ID to be present and match before resolving the binding.

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed selected-todo IDs before restoring
codex_findings.detail: When a v2 snapshot project carries a non-null, non-integer `selected_todo_id`, such as `"not-an-id"`, this raw value is written and `todo_store.restore()` subsequently clears it during reconciliation while the import reports success. That silently loses the project's explicitly chosen action instead of rejecting a corrupt or incompatible backup; require this field to be null or an integer before any store is written.

codex_findings.title: Preserve referenced projects during restore
codex_findings.detail: On any destination containing a `project_next_steps` or `deadlines` row—both declared with `REFERENCES projects(id)`—this unconditional deletion fails under `kitty_db.connect()`'s enabled foreign-key enforcement, even when importing a snapshot exported from the same database with identical project IDs. A self-export/import with a `project_next_steps` row produces `IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, blocking normal backup restoration; update existing parents in place or restore their dependents within the same transaction.

codex_findings.title: Preflight references to snapshot-omitted projects
codex_findings.detail: When restoring an older valid snapshot after a newer project has acquired a `project_next_steps` or `deadlines` row, this deletion hits foreign-key enforcement and aborts. Because `storage_sync.import_all()` has already appended memories and journal entries before calling `import_projects`, the failed restore leaves those earlier stores partially imported while retaining the current Projects state. Fresh evidence beyond the prior self-restore case is that an omitted newer project—not an ID present in both states—still takes this branch; validate or restore its dependents before earlier importers commit, or make the shared-SQLite restoration atomic.

codex_findings.title: Export projects and todos from one SQLite snapshot
codex_findings.detail: The live `/sync/export` path reads Projects and Todos through separate connections, although the newly exported `selected_todo_id` and todo ownership form one cross-table state. If a user selects or reassigns a todo between these two calls, the snapshot can contain the post-change todo owner but the pre-change project selection; import accepts that snapshot and silently restores without the user's selected action. Read both tables under one SQLite read transaction so the backup represents a coherent point in time.

codex_findings.title: Validate todos before committing restored projects
codex_findings.detail: When a v2 import reaches a todo error not covered by `_validate_snapshot_references`—for example duplicate `sort_order` values, duplicate IDs, or a write-time SQLite failure—this ordering has already committed the restored Projects. The request then raises while leaving Projects from the snapshot and Todos from the previous database; a duplicate-sort snapshot changes project data while preserving the old todo list. Prevalidate every todo invariant before any importer writes, or restore the shared SQLite stores in one transaction.

codex_findings.title: Preflight v1 todo owners against destination projects
codex_findings.detail: For an accepted v1 snapshot with no `projects` store, a todo can still carry the `project_id` exported by the previous format. If that project is absent on the destination, this condition skips reference validation, so `import_all()` commits memories and journal entries before `todo_store.restore()` raises for the unknown owner, leaving a partial restore. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier atomicity fix is this v1 compatibility path explicitly bypassing destination validation; preflight these owners against the destination project IDs before any importer runs.

codex_findings.title: Include projects before validating restored todo owners
codex_findings.detail: A normal export can contain todos assigned to user-created projects, but `storage_sync.export_all()` does not export or import the `projects` table. Restoring that valid snapshot into a fresh or rebuilt database therefore reaches this branch because only the seeded projects exist and aborts the entire todo restore with `unknown project_id`; a reproduced export containing project ID 3 fails exactly this way. Either include projects in the snapshot and restore them before todos, or otherwise define a round-trip-safe representation for these ownership links.

codex_findings.title: Reject non-integer todo IDs during restore
codex_findings.detail: When an imported todo carries a non-null, non-integer `id` such as `"1"`, this silently converts it to `None` and allocates a new ID. Because deleting todos does not reset SQLite's sequence, the import can report success with a different identity and then clear a project's `selected_todo_id` during reconciliation; this is reproducible with a selected todo whose string ID `"1"` is restored as ID 2. Reject malformed IDs before deleting existing rows instead of inventing a replacement identity.

codex_findings.title: Reject malformed project owners during restore
codex_findings.detail: If `/sync/import` receives a todo whose `project_id` is non-null but not an integer—for example the string `"3"`—prevalidation ignores it and this conversion silently stores `NULL`; the import reports success and can subsequently clear the project's selected-todo pointer, permanently dropping ownership rather than rejecting a corrupt or incompatible snapshot. Accept explicit null or an omitted field as unowned, but raise before `DELETE FROM todos` for every other type.

codex_findings.title: Recognize launchd-owned LiteLLM listeners
codex_findings.detail: On the supported macOS `./kitty install` path, launchd starts `/bin/bash <repo>/gateway/start_litellm.sh` and does not create `run/litellm.pid`. This classifier consults only that manual-launch pidfile (and its helper expects the different exact command `bash <path>`), so the LiteLLM child for the canonical launchd service remains reported as `external` in both status sections. Use `launchd_pid litellm` as an alternative verified controller and accept its actual command form so runtime provenance is truthful.
